papers.title: A short proof of the Segal conjecture for $C_p$
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of the generalized Segal conjecture for the cyclic group of prime order p, i.e. the fact that the Tate diagonal of any bounded below spectrum is a p-completion. The idea, inspired by Hahn and Wilson's argument, is to use descent along the equivariant map from the p-fold tensor power of the field with p elements to its topological Hochschild homology. The only computational input that we use is the calculation of the homotopy rings of this topological Hochschild homology and its Tate construction, together with the map induced by the cyclotomic Frobenius.

papers.title: On equivariant affineness in elliptic cohomology
papers.abstract:
We investigate equivariant affineness in spectral algebraic geometry: the phenomenon where $\infty$-categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of a spectral stack are equivalent to $\infty$-categories of modules over an equivariant ring spectrum. In the nonequivariant case, this is known as 0-affineness, and has been studied by Gaitsgory, Mathew--Meier, amongst others. Allowing for equivariant phenomena opens up a much wider class of spectral stacks to be studied through the lens of spectra.
  The spectral stacks at the heart of our analysis are oriented elliptic curves, their associated Hilbert schemes, and related constructions. When working over the universal base, so the moduli stack of oriented elliptic curves, we show that these spectral stacks are $U(1)$-, $U(n)$-, and $SU(n)$-equivariantly affine, with associated $G$-ring spectrum Gepner--Meier's equivariant topological modular forms $\mathrm{TMF}_G$. Our results also encompass the groups $Sp(n)$ as well as all finite products of such groups. Our most general result is a relative statement over an arbitrary base stack. These results can be viewed as an integral and global refinement of Greenlees' algebraic model for modules over rational $U(1)$-equivariant elliptic cohomology.

papers.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, reduced and immersed
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a `reduced' form of permutation twisted cohomology as introduced by Balmer--Gallauer and further developed by Miller. This ring is bigraded by a well-chosen choice of endotrivial complex, rather than multigraded by a family of endotrivial complexes. The Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules openly immerses into the homogeneous spectrum of this ring. We also show that for $p$-groups, Miller's `remixed' twisted cohomology ring also admits the Balmer spectrum as an open subspace, and confirm in both cases it can be upgraded to have Dirac scheme structure; furthermore, we prove that the two open covers witnessing this are in general different.

papers.title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
papers.abstract: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper \'etale correspondence $\Omega:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(\Omega)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.

papers.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
papers.abstract: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

papers.title: On the motivic approach to the Abhyankar rectifiability problem and concrete rectifications
papers.abstract: We study closed embeddings of the complex affine line into affine three-space. We prove that, for every such embedding, the complete-intersection normal map identifies the $\mathbb{A}^1$-fundamental sheaf of its complement with $\mathbf{K}_2^{\mathrm{MW}}$. The proof compares torsors under arbitrary strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves. A nodal projection expresses a torsor by a normal parameter and finitely many node parameters. Extension across the node axes gives equations for the latter. Their correction terms increase a nilpotent filtration generated by the Milnor-Witt symbols of the branch-height differences. We deduce the vanishing of the first Alexander sheaf of every complex embedded line. We also construct polynomial rectifications using finite inverses and affine modifications, including rectifications of the Shastri trefoil and a harmonic figure-eight over $\mathbb{Z}[a]/(a^2-a+1)$, with arbitrary base change. The companion repository (https://github.com/qft98romanov-hash/abhyankar-moh-trefoil) contains explicit rectifiers, their inverses, proofs, and symbolic checks. We prove that a normal map with a polynomial section and geometric generic affine-line fiber is a coordinate projection. We formulate the remaining rectifiability and descent questions; the general complex rectifiability problem is not settled here. An appendix treats other fields, normal orientations, and arithmetic descent.

papers.title: Models of n-dimensional categories as $n\to\infty$
papers.abstract: We verify that saturated complicial sets model the right limit of the $\infty$-categories of $(\infty,n)$-categories, whereas the canonical comparison with the left limit is not an equivalence. By contrast the category of strict $\omega$-categories is equivalent to both the right and left limits of the categories of strict $n$-categories.

papers.title: On strongly FP-injective accessibility and weakly FP-projective periodicity
papers.abstract: Accessibility results are established for (Cartan-Eilenberg) strongly FP-injective complexes, by first proving the accessibility of Strongly FP-injective modules and then utilizing the pseudopullback theorem. We also prove that every acyclic complex of weakly FP-projective modules has weakly FP-projective cycles over left $<\aleph_m$-coherent rings for a non-negative integer $m$. This is achieved by introducing the cotorsion pairs $\bigl(\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj,\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}inj\bigr)$, cogenerated by all $\aleph_m$-presentable weakly FP-projective modules, and proving that acyclic complexes of modules from the class $\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj$ have weakly FP-projective cycles for every non-negative integer $m$.

papers.title: Solid Arithmetic D-modules
papers.abstract: We introduce a solid ring of arithmetic differential operators analogue to Berthelot's D-dagger, and its derived infinity-category of solid quasi-coherent modules. We show that there is a fully faithful functor from Berthelot's derived category of bounded complexes of D-dagger-modules with coherent cohomology into our new category.

papers.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and give examples of smooth connected spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.

papers.title: The $6\frac{1}{2}$-functor formalism of Cartier modules
papers.abstract:
Let $p$ be a prime. We construct a coherent formalism of geometric operations on Cartier modules with coefficients in ind-coherent sheaves on noetherian derived $\mathbb F_p$-schemes. For such a scheme $X$, we consider the stable presentable category $\mathrm{Cart}(X)$ of ind-coherent sheaves $M$ equipped with a structural morphism $F_{*,X}M \to M$, where $F_X$ denotes the Frobenius endomorphism.
  We construct pushforward functors for arbitrary morphisms and exceptional pullback functors for separated morphisms almost of finite type, together with coherent composition and base-change equivalences. We single out conditions under which these functors admit further adjoints.
  On derived schemes separated and almost of finite type over $\mathbb F_p$, we construct compatible closed symmetric monoidal structures given by shriek tensor products, and establish which functors are symmetric monoidal.
  The constructions arise from a general procedure for forming functor formalisms of Cartier objects, using their description as lax limits and the universal properties of span $2$-categories developed by Cnossen--Lenz--Linskens [arXiv:2505.19192].

papers.title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Structure of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
papers.abstract:
We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups: for prime-power cyclic group equivariant, classes are represented by compatible vertex arrays or by edge arrays. In these coordinates we compute products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Then we assemble the results into arbitrary finite cyclic group equivariant case.
  Besides the computation, we also develop the Tate compression theory, which is used in the computation. The Tate compression diagram cut an equivariant spectra into several layer, which the homotopy group can be describe directly by each layers. From it we also give a filtration for $\pi_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}})$, compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

papers.title: Formality transmission
papers.abstract: Across mathematics, formality results are usually established through general criteria rather than by constructing explicit equivalences. These criteria include domination, puncturing, highly-connected formality, intrinsic formality, formality descent, formality in families, purity, etc. In this article, we prove that all these criteria are instances of a single theorem, formality transmission. This unifying framework allows us to extend these criteria in several directions, beyond characteristic zero and to differential graded algebras over operads or properads, leading to diverse new formality results.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
papers.abstract: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric. We prove that when $\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact connected embedded submanifold without boundary, with positive reach, and $\mathrm{A}\subset\mathcal{M}$ is a subset that is sufficiently dense in $\mathcal{M}$ with respect to the reach, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is bounded below by $1/2$ of the Hausdorff distance between them. We extend this result in two ways. First, we show that the factor $1/2$ can be improved using Jung's theorem. Second, we prove bounds on the Gromov-Hausdorff distance for pairs of subsets of $\mathcal{M}$. When $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ is equipped with the two-dimensional Euclidean metric, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ and any sufficiently dense subset of $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ can be expressed explicitly as a function of the Hausdorff distance between the two. We use interleavings between geometric simplicial complexes, nerve lemmas, properties of reach and the nearest-point projection map, and the fundamental class to produce the inequalities for general $\mathcal{M}$. We use the Borsuk-Ulam theorem for $\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{S}^1\subset \mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: Homotopy types and torsion in homology of generalized chessboard complexes
papers.abstract: Multiple chessboard complexes are deleted joins of skeleta of a simplex. We classify their homotopy types for at most three rows and extend this classification to arbitrary column capacities, with the $2$-torus as the only exception to a wedge of spheres. We determine explicit homotopy decompositions for two families with four and five rows and use a common capacity redistribution map to construct infinite families with $2$- and $3$-torsion in integral homology. Together, these results give a negative answer to the Segre part of the problem posed by Reiner and Roberts on characteristic-free resolutions of Segre and Veronese modules and identify three as the largest number of rows for which all generalized chessboard complexes have torsion-free integral homology. Our $3$-torsion construction applies to every square ordinary chessboard complex with at least five rows. Combined with earlier results, it completes the proof of the Shareshian-Wachs conjecture on torsion in chessboard complexes.

papers.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
papers.abstract: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth M\"obius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.

papers.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that all compact hyperk\"ahler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojevi\'c and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact K\"ahler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.

papers.title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
papers.abstract: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.

papers.title: Sheaves on quoric manifolds
papers.abstract: Quoric manifolds are quaternionic analogues of quasitoric manifolds introduced by Hopkinson. Given a quoric manifold over a simple polytope, we study the stratification induced by the faces of the polytope. We then show that the equivariant derived category of constructible sheaves with respect to the face stratification is equivalent to the derived category of constructible DG-modules over a DG-algebra defined on the orbit space. Finally, we prove that the associated DG-algebra is formal.

papers.title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
papers.abstract: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Sch\"utz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. We conjecture that the number of copies of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ equals the number of copies of $\mathbb{RP}^{2}\wedge\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in the even spectrum.

papers.title: The equal norm Grassmannian: topology and applications to frame fields
papers.abstract: Given an orientable rank-$d$ vector bundle over a $d$-manifold, the Euler class is the unique obstruction to finding a nowhere-zero section. An equal norm Parseval frame is a certain collection of sections, one of whose properties is that the lengths of each vector at each point are equal. This makes the Euler class an obvious obstruction to finding such a frame. In this work we show that this is the only obstruction so long as the number of sections is at least $2d+2$. We also identify precise obstructions when the number of sections is $2d$ and produce examples showing that for smaller numbers of sections it is sometimes impossible to find Parseval frame fields.

papers.title: The geometry of Floquet states
papers.abstract:
This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians.
  The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.

papers.title: The Oriented Freudenthal Suspension Theorem
papers.abstract: The Freudenthal Suspension Theorem states that the connectivity of the unit map $X\rightarrow\Omega\Sigma X$ of the suspension-loop adjunction for a pointed space $X$ is twice the connectivity of $X$ itself. We extend this theorem to $X$ being a pointed $(\infty,\infty)$-category, i.e. an oriented space in the sense of Gepner--Heine.

papers.title: The Segal conjecture for large objects and semiadditive lifts
papers.abstract:
We prove a projection formula for homotopy fixed points of trivial actions of finite $p$-groups. More precisely, for every bounded-below, $p$-complete spectrum $X$ whose mod-$p$ homology is $I$-complete, the canonical map \[ (\mathbb S_p)^{BG}\otimes X \overset{\simeq}{\rightarrow} X^{BG} \] is an equivalence for every finite $p$-group $G$, where $I$ is the augmentation ideal of the Steenrod algebra.
  Building on earlier joint work with Burklund, our proof combines the Adams--Gunawardena--Miller calculation with an adaptation of Carlsson's induction. As an application, using the work of Yuan, we construct height-one semiadditive lifts of such spectra and show that their cohomology of $p$-finite spaces depends only on the $1$-type.

papers.title: Analytic Kasparov product for non-separable C$^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We develop an analytic framework for the explicit construction of Kasparov products on uncountably generated Hilbert modules over non-separable C$^*$-algebras by extending the classical Kasparov bimodule picture. In particular, this yields a well-defined functor from the category of general C$^*$-algebras whose restriction to separable C$^*$-algebras coincides with classical KK-theory and which satisfies several properties expected of non-separable KK-theory. A key idea of the extension is to replace a single Fredholm operator on a Kasparov bimodule with a net and to encode the directed system of separable C$^*$-subalgebras. We also introduce the notion of freely complementable Hilbert modules and develop cropping techniques to extend Kasparov's technical theorem beyond the countably generated setting. It naturally gives rise to a sufficiently broad class of C$^*$-algebras that provides a non-commutative analogue of paracompactness and includes all $\sigma$-unital algebras.

papers.title: On the cohomological dimension of Henselian valued fields
papers.abstract: Let $(K,v)$ be a Henselian valued field of rank one and of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with value group $\Gamma$ dense in $\mathbb{R}$ and residue field $k$. We compute all the graded pieces of the filtration induced by $v$ on the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ of $K$, in terms of the exterior powers of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector space $\Gamma/p\Gamma$ and of the modules of differential forms of $k$. This extends to the non-discrete setting a classical theorem of Kato concerning complete discretely valued fields. We also prove that, when $(K,v)$ is maximally complete, no class escapes this filtration by accumulating at a limit. As an application, we prove the inequality $\dim_p(K)\geq\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\Gamma/p\Gamma)+\dim_p(k)$ between Kato's $p$-dimensions, and we show that it becomes an equality as soon as $(K,v)$ is maximally complete.

papers.title: $C_2$-cofiniteness of finite-group orbifolds
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a simple vertex algebra with a connected nonnegative integer grading, and let $G$ be a finite group of grading-preserving automorphisms. We prove that $C_2$-cofiniteness of $V$ implies $C_2$-cofiniteness of $V^G$. The proof bounds the length and height of monomials in strong generators representing classes in a relative $C_2$ quotient. The length bound follows from a good filtration and finite-group invariant theory. The height bound follows from differential equations for products of fields, together with identities for invariants and vacuum coefficients. The height bound also shows that finite strong generation passes to $V^G$, without assuming $C_2$-cofiniteness. For strongly rational vertex operator algebras, the cofiniteness result and McRae's orbifold theorem imply strong rationality of every finite-group fixed-point algebra.

papers.title: A Boolean Lévy group with a free nonsingular action
papers.abstract: We construct a Boolean Lévy group with a free ergodic spatial nonsingular action on a standard probability space, answering a question of Glasner, Tsirelson and Weiss. The action admits no equivalent invariant $\sigma$-finite measure. The group is a quotient of a weighted summable Boolean group by a discrete subgroup. By the nonsingular fixed-point theorem of Avraham-Re'em and Peterzil, the resulting group is not locally Wasserstein.

papers.title: A bridge between analysis on local fields and quantum groups: the compact case
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field with residue cardinality $Q$ and let $d \geq 1$. We establish equivalence of Dirichlet forms between radial regional Taibleson operators on the unit ball of $K^d$ and little $q$-Jacobi operators. Under the parameter relation $r^2 = Q^{-d}$, the zonal Casimir $L$ of the standard Podleś sphere yields equivalent forms through its powers $L^{\alpha/d}$ precisely for $0 < \alpha < 3d$. Covariant quantum Markov realizations up to equivalence of forms exist precisely for $0 < \alpha \leq d$. We also relate this correspondence to boundary energies: harmonic extensions on the tree of balls recover a Taibleson energy, while the energy per level of quantum Poisson integrals converges to a multiple of the Casimir energy. Finally, we extend the correspondence and the sharp covariance threshold to quantum projective spaces, identifying the Taibleson orders associated with their zonal Casimir operators.

papers.title: A bridge between analysis on local fields and quantum groups: the noncompact case
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field with residue cardinality $Q$ and let $d \geq 1$. We establish a radial correspondence between analysis on $K^d$ and Woronowicz's quantum group $\mathrm{E}_r(2)$, with $r^2 = Q^{-d}$. For every $\alpha > 0$, the radial Taibleson operator of order $\alpha$ is unitarily equivalent, through a unitary commuting with dilations, to a bilateral birth–death operator with Hahn–Exton $q$-Bessel eigenfunctions. Their Dirichlet forms are equivalent on the same weighted sequence space, with optimal comparison constants. For $\alpha = d$, the bilateral operator is the radial part of a self-adjoint Casimir on the quantum plane $\mathrm{E}_r(2)/\mathbb{T}$, whose heat semigroup is covariant and completely positive. We further obtain these quantum-plane dynamics by contraction of the compact Casimir dynamics on the Podleś sphere, with Mosco convergence of the forms and pointwise norm convergence of the compressed heat maps.

papers.title: A curve of genus $2$ over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and hexads of bitangents to a smooth quartic
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the Abel-Jacobi map of a genus 2 curve over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ arising from a double cover of $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ branched along six lines. We utilize the so-called Mumford representations to conduct the calculations. As an application, we give an alternative proof of classical results on quartics and bitangents. Furthermore, we obtain a method to give explicit defining equations of quartic curves that have the six lines as bitangents and apply it to determine the number of connected components of the realization space.

papers.title: A dynamical approach to Frobenius splitting
papers.abstract:
A dynamical system can be associated to the process of decomposing iterated Frobenius pushforwards of modules into indecomposable direct summands. Via this connection, we apply the theory of Markov chains to study asymptotic counts of multiplicities of indecomposable summands in the iterated Frobenius pushforwards of the given module, as the number of iterations grows. Our results recover and extend the existing results on the existence of the (generalized) F-signature due to Hashimoto--Symonds, Hashimoto--Kobayashi, Smith--Van den Bergh, Tucker, and Yao. We also develop further the theory of F-contributors, the modules for which the multiplicity grows at the maximal possible rate.
  As a key algebraic input, we define and develop strongly F-regular modules, extending Hochster--Huneke's notion of strongly F-regular rings. We use strongly F-regular modules to prove convergence of the relevant sequences and algebraically characterize F-contributors, when the underlying ring admits a module-finite strongly F-regular extension or has dimension at most two.

papers.title: A finiteness result for split exceptional dual pairs
papers.abstract: We prove that big theta lifts have finite length for thirteen split exceptional dual pairs arising from the minimal representations of the split real groups of types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$.

papers.title: A Gasch\"utz Lemma for linear algebraic groups with applications to the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
papers.abstract: The classical Gasch\"utz Lemma states that for a surjective morphism $G\to H$ of finite groups, generators $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ of $H$ can be lifted to generators $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ of $G$, provided that $G$ can be generated by $d$ elements. We prove an analog of this statement for linear algebraic groups. This has applications to the algebraic-geometric theory of linear differential equations: We show that every regular singular differential embedding problem over the rational function field has a regular singular solution. We also establish a purely algebraic variant of the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence on the punctured projective line that works over any countable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.

papers.title: A groupoid approach to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a groupoid approach to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture. For a bounded geometry metric space $X$ equipped with a proper, free, and isometric action of a countable discrete group $\Gamma$, we introduce the equivariant coarse groupoid $G(X, \Gamma)$. We prove that the groupoid Baum--Connes conjecture for $G(X, \Gamma)$ with coefficients in $\ell^{\infty}(X,\K)^\Ga$ is equivalent to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture for $(X, \Gamma)$ using a localization algebra description of groupoid equivariant $KK$-theory on the Rips complex models. As applications of this framework, we prove that if the space $X$ admits a coarse embedding into Hilbert space (which is not required to be $\Gamma$-equivariant), then the equivariant coarse Novikov conjecture holds for $(X, \Gamma)$, i.e., the assembly map $\mu_{X,\Ga}$ is an injection. We also obtain a new proof of the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture if $X$ admits an equivariant coarse embedding into Hilbert space.

papers.title: A lattice-theoretic approach to the abc conjecture: Weighted arithmetic derivatives, a master inequality, and the structure of the residual family
papers.abstract: We develop a self-contained lattice-theoretic framework for the abc conjecture. For coprime positive integers $a+b=c$ with $k=\omega(ab)$, the framework rests on a weighted arithmetic derivative $d^\psi$ whose additivity equation $d^\psi(a+b)=d^\psi(a)+d^\psi(b)$ is solvable modulo the modulus $g_c=\gcd_{p\parallel c}\bigl(\frac{c}{p}v_p(c)\bigr)$, and on a Wronskian identity $W=a\,d^\psi(b)-b\,d^\psi(a)=M_{ab}\,H(u)$, where $M_{ab}=ab/\operatorname{rad}(ab)$ and $H$ is an explicit linear form. A divisibility lemma $M_aM_bM_c\mid W$ and an elementary upper bound yield the master inequality $c\le\mu_{ab}\cdot\frac{\Omega(ab)}{2}\cdot\operatorname{rad}(abc)$, in which the defect factor $\mu_{ab}$ is the shortest non-kernel weight of an explicit solution lattice $\Lambda$ of determinant $g_c/g$. Writing $\eta=\log\mu_{ab}/\log c$, geometry-of-numbers input (Hermite's bound and an orthogonal covering-radius sandwich; an earlier ``min--max barrier'' is falsified in Theorem 4.5) yields, conditionally on an explicit gap hypothesis $(\star')$ isolated in Section 7, the bound $\eta\le\frac1k+o(1)$, whence $\limsup_{c\to\infty}q(a,b,c)\le\frac{k}{k-1}\le2$, i.e.\ $c\lesssim\operatorname{rad}(abc)^{2+o(1)}$. On the subclass $a+b=r^e$ the method closes unconditionally (Zsigmondy for $r\ge3$; cyclotomic/LTE control of valuations for $a=1$). The residual family is localized by a power--congruence bridge: $q^V\parallel b$ forces $e$ into a single residue class modulo $d\,q^{V-s}$ ($d=\operatorname{ord}_q(r)$, $s$ the Wieferich depth), of convergent total density; the unique unclosed layer reduces to growth-difference Pillai-type equations. We also prove a structural ceiling: the main term of $\eta$ is at most $\frac1k+o(1)$ and attains $\frac1k$ on the family $c=r^e$, so the full abc conjecture ($q\le1+\varepsilon$) is structurally unreachable inside this framework. A final section determines the reach and limits of the method elementarily: almost all $c$ have every coprime decomposition with $q\le1+o(1)$ (density theorem, by one-variable counting, exceptional set $\ll X^{1/2+o(1)}$), while any argument within the method class $\mathcal M$ cannot prove $\limsup q\le\alpha$ for any $\alpha<2$ (obstacle theorem), and the only remaining channel is equivalent to a sparse growth-difference Pillai core. All statements are proved in full or are explicitly labelled as working hypotheses; numerical cross-checks from two independent implementations are included, and no claim of a proof of the abc conjecture is made.

papers.title: A lower bound for the sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function
papers.abstract: We prove that the lower limit of the sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function, normalized by $(a_3/9!)T(\log T)^9$, is greater than $41.007$. Our approach extends the two-piece amplifier construction used by Durkan and Page by allowing independent profiles, centered derivatives, and finite real linear combinations of two projected test families. An asymmetric twisted fourth-moment estimate and their amplified moment formula yield a common numerator kernel. Explicit balanced and unbalanced kernels determine the projected Gram form. A rational certificate with 250 tests, followed by approximation by admissible profiles, gives the stated bound.

papers.title: A Proof of McLeod's 1959 Conjecture on Complete Homogeneous Symmetric Ratios
papers.abstract: We prove McLeod's (1959) conjecture that $(h_{\ell+r}/h_\ell)^{1/r}$ is subadditive for all $\ell\ge0$ and $r\ge1$, where $h_k$ is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial of degree $k$ (J. B. McLeod, "On four inequalities in symmetric functions", Proc. Edinburgh Math. Soc., 1959). We first prove that the ratio $h_k/h_{k-1}$ is convex, and our proof takes an unexpected detour through queuing theory. The geometric mean of $r$ consecutive such ratios equals McLeod's conjectured function, but geometric means of convex functions need not be convex. Our second and decisive step is a tensorization trick that couples neighboring ratios tightly enough to make their geometric mean convex.

papers.title: A Spectral Blakley–Roy Inequality for Nonnegative Matrices
papers.abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be real symmetric matrices with nonnegative entries. We prove that $\rho(AB)^k\le\rho(A^kB^k)$ for the spectral radius $\rho(\cdot)$ and every integer $k\ge1$; for $B=uu^T$ this is the Blakley–Roy inequality. We prove it via the more general inequality $\|(AB)^m\|^{k}\le\|(A^kB^k)^m\|$ in the spectral norm, valid for all integers $k,m\ge1$. The even exponents case follows from standard tools; for odd exponents $k=2r+1$ the claim follows via the more general product inequality $(u^TC_1\cdots C_tv)^k\le(u^Tu)^r(v^Tv)^r\,u^TC_1^k\cdots C_t^kv$ for nonnegative symmetric $C_i$ and nonnegative $u,v$. Its proof is an entropy argument on paths that traverse each edge $k$ times, back and forth.

papers.title: A true theorem Lean can state but can never verify
papers.abstract: We give an expository account of a mathematical result that the Lean proof assistant can formally state but, by Gödel's second incompleteness theorem, can never verify, and which it also does not refute, namely, the consistency of Lean's own underlying type theory. Working in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ extended by the existence of infinitely many inaccessible cardinals, we sketch the construction of a set-theoretic model of Lean's Calculus of Inductive Constructions (with its universe hierarchy, quotient types, and choice), outline the proof of a soundness lemma, and conclude that no derivation of $\mathtt{False}$ exists. The argument is the model-theoretic consistency proof carried out in full by Carneiro, building on Werner's set-theoretic interpretation of the same calculus; all substantive results are due to these authors, and this paper claims no new mathematics. We explain why this theorem lies outside Lean's own reach, note that Gödel's second incompleteness theorem has itself been verified by Lean's kernel for first-order arithmetic, and discuss why every consistency proof ultimately rests on trust rather than proof.

papers.title: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves
papers.abstract: We study the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes from genus-two curves over finite fields. Let $C_\mathcal{ L}(D,G)$ be such a code over $\mathbb F_q$, with length $n$ and dimension $k$. Assume that $3\leq k\leq n-3$. We prove that $n<(2q+10\sqrt q+16)/3$. This bound holds for every prime power $q$ and for both parities of $k$. It gives a uniform upper bound of $2q/3+O(\sqrt q)$ for the maximal length. The explicit bound is strictly smaller than $q+1$ when $q\geq125$.

papers.title: A Yau-Tian-Donaldson correspondence for degenerations
papers.abstract:
We prove an equivalence between the existence of a unique K\"ahler-Einstein metric on a degeneration of Fano varieties and uniform CM minimization. This proves a discretely valued analogue of the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture, in the sense of non-Archimedean geometry.
  As a main tool, we prove that Ding stability of a degeneration implies uniform Ding minimization, proving a converse to work of Blum-Xu. We also prove an analogous result in geometric invariant theory (GIT), stating that uniform GIT height minimization of a family of points is equivalent to GIT stability, proving a converse to work of Wang, Wang-Xu and the author.

papers.title: Abelian Orbifolds for Brane Brick Models
papers.abstract: We present a systematic procedure for constructing brane brick models corresponding to abelian orbifolds of toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds, extending the orbifold construction beyond the well-studied case of abelian orbifolds of C^4. Given a parent brane brick model corresponding to a toric Calabi-Yau 4-fold M, we show that the action of an abelian orbifold group Gamma on the generators of M induces an action on the chiral and Fermi fields as well as the J- and E-terms of the associated 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theory. The requirement that the orbifolded brane brick model remains consistent with the closed paths associated with the J- and E-terms, together with the chiral cycles formed by their products, precisely reproduces the Calabi-Yau condition on the orbifold action. This procedure yields an explicit formula for the J- and E-terms of the orbifolded brane brick model in terms of those of the parent theory. We apply our construction to the brane brick models corresponding to Q^{1,1,1} and D_3, and present the resulting families of 2d (0,2) quiver gauge theories. We also present explicit expressions for generating functions that count distinct abelian orbifolds of Q^{1,1,1} and D_3.

papers.title: Affinizations and braided module categories
papers.abstract: We relate affinizations of braided monoidal categories to braided module categories, allowing a twist by a braided monoidal automorphism. Our main theorem establishes a bijection between twisted braided structures on a right module category and extensions of its action to the corresponding twisted affinization. We also show that the twisted affinization is the free twisted braided module category on one object. We give explicit presentations of twisted affinizations, both as monoidal categories and as module categories, using invertible dots and reflection relations. We also describe the relation to cylinder twists and tensor-pair cylinder twists, including the naturality condition needed to obtain a braided module structure. As applications, we obtain module-category presentations of the affine Kauffman and affine oriented skein categories and an orientation-reversing twisted version of the latter. We realize the disoriented skein category as a quotient of this twisted affinization by a single additional relation.

papers.title: Algebraicity of rank-two scattering wall functions
papers.abstract: We prove that every wall function in the rank-two scattering factorization determined by two polynomial initial walls over a field of characteristic zero is algebraic. This resolves the algebraicity question posed by Kontsevich and recorded by Gross and Pandharipande, and its cluster-scattering formulation in the work of Burcroff, Lee, Mou, Musiker, and Reineke.

papers.title: Amitsur groups of Imprimitive Fano Threefolds
papers.abstract: We classify possible Amitsur groups of smooth imprimitive Fano threefolds defined over $\cc$ that admit a faithful action of a finite group.

papers.title: Amplituhedra and origami, I: tree level
papers.abstract: We establish a precise correspondence between points of the $m=4$ tree momentum amplituhedron and origami crease patterns. As an application, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ tree amplituhedron both in momentum space and in momentum-twistor space. As another application, we show that every nondegenerate weighted planar bipartite graph $\Gamma$ admits a t-embedding, i.e., an embedding of the planar dual of $\Gamma$ such that the sum of angles of white (equivalently, black) faces around each vertex is equal to $\pi$.

papers.title: Amplituhedra and origami, II: loop level
papers.abstract: Building on the recently discovered origami-amplituhedron correspondence, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ amplituhedron in full generality at all loop orders, both in momentum and momentum-twistor space. Along the way, we develop two natural "$L$-punctured" extensions of the positive Grassmannian and relate them via T-duality.

papers.title: An analogue of $\Gamma$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $\Gamma$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.

papers.title: An Arithmetic Property of Intertwining Operators for Real Reductive Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of complex points of a connected split reductive group defined over ${\mathbb Q}$. We study the standard intertwining operator between representations parabolically induced from essentially tempered cohomological representations of Levi subgroups of maximal parabolic subgroups. Under certain algebraicity, purity, and criticality hypotheses, the operator is holomorphic and invertible at a particular point of evaluation. The relative Lie algebra cohomology of these induced representations is one-dimensional in the lowest nonzero degree. Under prescribed rational generators of these one-dimensional spaces, we show that the intertwining operator is a nonzero rational multiple of a certain product of ratios of local $L$-factors. This is a cohomological version of Langlands's calculation of the Gindikin-Karplevic formula. The main theorem provides a local input for the arithmetic study of special values of Langlands--Shahidi $L$-functions.

papers.title: An improved zero-free half-plane for Hecke L-functions over number fields and Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain a zero-free half-plane Re(s) > B∗ for every finite-order Hecke L- function over every number field, where B∗ = 0.87446830769353045955... is an explicitly defined algebraic number. This improves the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis over arbitrary num- ber fields. The proof refines the cubic-theta comparison. A sharper amplified Gauss-norm estimate permits a longer additional prime product, chosen separately for each dyadic sum- mation length. Combining the resulting moment saving with contour displacement on the same dyadic sum gives the principal improvement. The enlarged moment controls the critical summation length, where the contour contribution vanishes. Successive improvements of the character-counting estimate then reach the algebraic endpoint, while the numerator-moment parameter remains fixed. We prove optimality within the resulting comparison system. The argument uses the established theta, moment and continuation results of the earlier QRH papers and the general-field formulation of those results.

papers.title: An Integral-Structure Inflation in the Hull Operation of IUT Corollary 3.12
papers.abstract: This paper identifies and rigorously quantifies a third-class gap in the passage from Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 in S. Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmuller theory (IUT). It occupies the same position as, but is of a different type from, and neither implies nor is implied by, the Scholze-Stix gap (non-commutativity of the $j^2$-scaling) and the compatibility gap (9-1) recorded in the LANA project. The holomorphic hull of IUT III, Remark 3.9.5, is the minimum over the constrained family $\{\lambda \cdot \mathcal{O}\}$: each direct summand of $I^{\mathbb{Q}} \cong \bigoplus_{\alpha} F_{\alpha}$ is scaled independently. This operation "boxes" the image of the tensor-product integral structure and introduces an index $\rho$. The main mathematical result of this paper is the exact closed form of this index, $\rho = |\mathfrak{d}_K|^{(n-1)d^{n-1}/2}$, $d = [K:\mathbb{Q}_p]$, proved as an identity of positive integers (not merely a $p$-adic valuation), where $\mathfrak{d}_K$ is the discriminant of $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$. Its $p$-adic corollary is $v_p(\rho) = \frac{(n-1)d^{n-1}}{2}\, v_p(\mathfrak{d}_K)$: the loss equals $\frac{n-1}{2}$ times (number of components) times (the $p$-adic valuation of the local discriminant). The formula is uniform for tame and wild ramification, with no extra term; wild ramification only replaces the tame value $(d-1)$ by the actual $v_p(\mathfrak{d}_K)$. Substituting IUT's own parameters ($n = j+1$, $\ell^* = (\ell-1)/2 \asymp h^{1/2}$, $v \in V^{\mathrm{bad}}$), the inflation is doubly exponential: $\log\log\rho = \Theta(\sqrt{h})$, i.e. $\rho = \exp(\exp(\Theta(\sqrt{h})))$. Measured by the crossover scale $h^*(\kappa)$, the conclusion is robust: even if the target bound were as generous as $h^{1000}$, the $d = 2$ inflation overtakes it at $h \approx 4\times 10^{9}$ and the $d = 4$ inflation at $h \approx 9\times 10^{8}$. This paper is not a verdict on IUT. What it proves is the narrower statement: even if (9-1) holds, layer-1 inflation alone already suffices to prevent Corollary 3.12 from yielding abc.

papers.title: An Unexpected Rational Blowdown
papers.abstract: The rational blowdown operation in 4-manifold topology replaces a neighborhood of a configuration of spheres by a rational homology ball. Such configurations typically arise from resolutions of surface singularities that admit rational homology disk smoothings. Conjecturally, all such singularities must be weighted homogeneous and belong to certain specific families: Stipsicz-Szab\'o--Wahl constructed QHD smoothings for these families and used Donaldson's theorem to obtain very restrictive necessary conditions on the resolution graphs for singularities with this property. In particular, these results, as well as subsequent work of Bhupal-Stipsicz, show that for certain resolution graphs, the canonical contact structure on the link of the singularity cannot admit a QHD symplectic filling. By contrast, we exhibit Stein rational homology disk fillings for the contact links of an infinite family of rational singularities that are not weighted homogeneous, producing a new symplectic rational blowdown. Inspiration for our construction comes from de Jong-van Straten's description of Milnor fibers of sandwiched singularities; we use the symplectic analog of de Jong-van Straten theory developed by the second and third authors. The unexpected Stein fillings are built using spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations.

papers.title: Analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient Toda systems: W-invariants and Weyl orbits
papers.abstract: We classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient Toda systems for all simple Lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. We encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the Cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_\mu$ and the mass element $q_\sigma$. We show that $p_\mu-q_\sigma=wp_\mu$ for some Weyl group element $w\in W$. The proof uses the Drinfeld-Sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $W$-invariants for Toda systems. Asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading Laurent coefficients of the $W$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. This agreement enables us to conclude the above Weyl-orbit result. In particular, the quadratic constraint is the local Pohozaev identity. Only with the full set of $W$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact Weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. Together with the author's explicit families in [Nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.

papers.title: Analytic symmetric floating bodies
papers.abstract: In every dimension $d\ge3$, we construct nonspherical, origin-symmetric, strictly convex bodies of revolution with real-analytic boundary that float in equilibrium in every orientation. Their densities tend to the unit-ball cap fraction at height $(d+4)^{-1/2}$, where we prove that a degree-four spherical resonance is isolated. More generally, our construction applies at isolated even-degree resonances whose waterline angle is an irrational multiple of $\pi$. Varying the density gives formal deformations. To obtain actual bodies, we use a finite-order diagonal reduction to establish inverse estimates away from small divisors. Newton iteration then corrects fixed-order truncations on closed parameter sets of asymptotically full measure.

papers.title: Anti-Zariski pairs
papers.abstract: In 1929, O. Zariski found a pair of complex plane algebraic curves of the same degree and with the same collection of singularities, but embedded into the plane in a topologically different way. Accordingly, such curves belong to different components of the equisingular family. This phenomenon has been intensively studied till now. In this note, we propose a different insight on this subject: Two curves $C',C''\subset\PP^2$ form an {\it anti-Zariski pair}, if $(\PP^2,C')$ and $(\PP^2,C'')$ are homeomorhic, but $C'$ and $C''$ belong to different components of the equisingular family. We exhibit examples of anti-Zariski pairs and discuss related issues.

papers.title: Approximation of adelic divisors and equidistribution of small points
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the Galois orbits of generic sequences of algebraic points of small height in a projective variety over a number field. Our main result is a generalization of Yuan's equidistribution theorem that applies to heights for which Zhang's lower bound for the essential minimum is not necessarily an equality. It extends to all projective varieties a theorem of Burgos Gil, Philippon, Rivera-Letelier and the second author for toric varieties. It also applies to sums of canonical heights for an algebraic dynamical system, and in particular it recovers K\"uhne's semiabelian equidistribution theorem. We also generalize previous work of Chambert-Loir and Thuillier to obtain new logarithmic equidistribution results. Finally we extend our main result to the quasi-projective setting recently introduced by Yuan and Zhang.

papers.title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
papers.abstract: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

papers.title: Archimedean Modular Symbols for Rankin-Selberg Convolutions of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$
papers.abstract: We explicit calculate the archimedean modular symbol for Rankin-Selberg convolutions of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$, for all generic cohomological representations.

papers.title: Archimedean period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions
papers.abstract: We formulate and prove the archimedean period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions of $\text{GL}(n)\times \text{GL}(n)$ and $\text{GL}(n)\times \text{GL}(n-1)$, for all generic cohomological representations. As a consequence, we prove the non-vanishing of the archimedean modular symbols. This extends the earlier results in [LLS24] for essentially tempered representations of $\text{GL}(n)\times\text{GL}(n-1)$.

papers.title: Asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ of stable pointed curves and the all-light Hassett spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0|n}$, for fixed genus $g\ge1$ as the number of markings tends to infinity. We prove central limit theorems for the full Betti distributions, whose variances grow linearly in $n$ with leading coefficients independent of the genus. For the normalized even Betti numbers, we establish refined local limit theorems with estimates uniform in degree. These local estimates yield asymptotic formulas for individual even Betti numbers and determine the sharp central ultra-log-concavity thresholds $\frac{3(e-2)}{2(3-e)}$ and $3$, respectively. For $g\ge2$, the off-diagonal Hodge components form proportions of exact orders $n^{-1/2}$ and $n^{-1}$ of the total cohomology of the two spaces, respectively. The conditional distributions of the Hodge difference $p-q$ given $p\ne q$ converge, for both spaces, to a single discrete law independent of the genus. We also prove that tautological classes account for all but a proportion of exact order $n^{-1}$ of the even cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$. The tautological degree distribution converges to the standard Gaussian under the centering and scaling of the ambient even Betti distribution. An explicit asymptotic formula for the ratio of the ordinary Euler characteristics of the light and heavy spaces answers a question of Kannan, Serpente and Yun. The proofs combine the heavy/light substitution with a stratification of the light spaces by stable cores, singularity analysis of Hodge generating functions, and refined Fourier estimates exploiting Poincar\'e duality.

papers.title: Asymptotic GIT-stability of KSB-stable varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that KSB-stable varieties introduced by Koll\'ar and Shepherd-Barron as a generalization of Deligne-Mumford's stable curves are stable in the sense of geometric invariant theory (GIT). More precisely, we show that KSB-stable varieties are asymptotically GIT-stable with respect to a sequence of linearizations defined by the Hodge bundle.

papers.title: Asymptotic growth of rank-two scattering coefficients in the Badlands
papers.abstract: We prove that the normalized logarithmic growth rate of ordinary wall-function coefficients in every wild rank-two cluster scattering diagram exists along all integer approaches to an interior Badlands slope and is continuous in that slope. This resolves Conjecture 9.2 of Burcroff, Lee, Mou, Musiker, and Reineke.

papers.title: Automated Conjecturing: Generation, Selection and Evaluation
papers.abstract: Deciding which conjectures are worth proving is a crucial part of mathematical discovery, and a system that learns mathematics from its axioms alone must make that decision without human guidance. Self-play provers such as Minimo learn a conjecturer alongside the prover and reward it for producing hard conjectures, but a conjecture that is harder to prove is not necessarily more useful for improving a prover: the learned conjecturer drifts toward long, artificial statements. We study conjecturing in a controlled, single-round setting in the Peano formal environment, across propositional logic, abelian groups, and natural-number multiplication, evaluating a set of conjectures by how much a fixed prover improves on held-out theorems after training on their proofs. We show that a far simpler generator does better: making small structural edits to statements the prover already knows yields conjectures that, at an equal training budget and under best-first search, improve the prover by 6 to 13 percentage points more than Minimo's learned conjectures. The gain holds even when conjectures are drawn at random from the generated pool. In contrast to the common practice of selecting the most difficult statements, we also propose Hard Neighbours (HN), a score that favors conjectures whose proof difficulty grows disproportionately relative to their structural distance from easier reference statements; HN gives the largest selection gains in propositional logic, but no selection method is best in every domain. In the current setting, how conjectures are generated matters more than how they are selected, and structural perturbation is the baseline that future conjecturers should be measured against. Apart from improvements in proving ability, we also study other attributes of generated proofs: the amount of search required and the length of the proofs.

papers.title: Automorphism groups of smooth quartic threefolds
papers.abstract: We classify finite groups of automorphisms of smooth quartic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$. Every such group embeds into one of $17$ maximal groups, which we realize by explicit equations and matrix generators. Among finite subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}(5,\mathbb{C})$ preserving a smooth quartic threefold, there are exactly $24$ maximal ones up to conjugacy, and we use them to determine the $194$ groups that occur as full automorphism groups. As an application, we classify the finite groups of projective automorphisms of smooth quartic surfaces and show that there are exactly $12$ maximal ones up to conjugacy in $\mathrm{PGL}(4,\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: Bad Reduction of Genus Two Curves with complex multiplication
papers.abstract: We study genus two curves whose Jacobians have complex multiplication by a biquadratic CM field. In this setting the Jacobian decomposes as a product of two elliptic curves with complex multiplication by orders in the same imaginary quadratic field. We derive upper bounds for the primes of stable bad reduction of such curves in terms of the discriminants of the CM orders. To do so, we give an explicit description of principally polarized abelian surfaces with CM by a biquadratic field via small CM cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety of signature (3,2). We use it to prove an arithmetic intersection formula between such CM cycles with Humbert surfaces in terms of coefficients of incoherent Eisenstein series and representation numbers of ternary positive definite quadratic forms. Finally, employing the arithmetic properties of higher Green functions, we show that primes of stable bad reduction always exist.

papers.title: Balancing tautological intersection numbers
papers.abstract: We prove the three balancing inequalities conjectured by the authors about 20 years ago: moving one unit from a larger index to a smaller one cannot decrease a mixed tautological intersection number, whether the two distinguished insertions are psi classes, kappa classes, or Hodge Chern classes.

papers.title: Bases for the Top-Degree Garsia-Haiman Module
papers.abstract: We introduce two new monomial bases for the top $t$-degree component of the Garsia-Haiman module $V_\mu$ for every partition $\mu$. Both bases are indexed by column-strict standard fillings of shape $\mu$; the first has exponents governed by entrywise refinements of Haglund's combinatorial statistics for the modified Macdonald polynomials $\widetilde{H}_\mu(X;q,t)$. The second basis has exponents governed by an insertion algorithm of Bhattacharya-Ratheesh-Viswanath, and gives a basis realization of the ``fermionic formula" of the $m_{1^n}$-coefficient of the $q$-Whittaker polynomial. Our proof uses orbit harmonics, and is inspired by the original approach of Garsia and Haiman.

papers.title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
papers.abstract:
We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two. Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle.
  More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic N\'eron--Severi lattice. The key new result is the congruence property of the subgroup generated by reflective involutions in $O(U\oplus N)$ for anisotropic even lattices $N$ of signature $(1,1)$. Combined with the local generation theorem and Chow-theoretic criterion of Li--Yu--Zhang, this gives the required reflective decompositions and their consequences for zero-cycles.

papers.title: Borel subalgebras of Lie algebras of vector fields
papers.abstract: In [I. Arzhantsev and M. Zaidenberg, Borel subgroups of the automorphism groups of affine toric surfaces, arXiv:2507.09679 (2025)] we described the Borel subgroups and maximal solvable subgroups of the automorphism groups of affine toric surfaces. In the present paper, we introduce the notion of an integrable Borel subalgebra in the Lie algebra of the automorphism group of an affine variety. We show that they are precisely the tangent algebras of the Borel subgroups. We classify the integrable Borel subalgebras in the Lie algebras of the automorphism groups of toric affine surfaces, notably of the affine plane and its cyclic quotients.

papers.title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact K\"ahler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-K\"ahler nature of this notion. We also investigate different techniques for constructing examples of such manifolds. Finally, we examine the relationship between Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity and Kobayashi hyperbolicity in the examples considered, highlighting obstructions to the latter in the Calabi--Yau setting.

papers.title: Categorical Tiling Theory: Constructing Directed Planar Tilings via Edge Reversal
papers.abstract: Tilings of the plane resemble the simplicial and other complexes from algebraic topology, but have not been studied from this perspective. We construct finite categories corresponding to polygons with labeled directed edges, and introduce the problem of modeling tilings of the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane as presheaves over such a category. Combinatorially, this amounts to choosing an ``alignment'' for a tiling: a direction for every edge and consistent labels for the edges of each polygonal tile. We show that for a fixed tiling, given a single alignment we can characterize every other alignment of the same tiling by comparison of the edge directions. We then construct a ``reflective'' alignment for any tiling with an even number of polygons at each vertex, and from this generate a large family of alignments with elegant symmetry properties.

papers.title: Categorification in Representation Theory
papers.abstract: In this survey article, we give an introduction to the relatively young subject of $2$-representation theory, which studies categorifications of important players in classical representation theory. In particular, we provide a streamlined exposition of the main results leading to the classification of simple $2$-representations for Soergel bimodules associated to finite Weyl groups in characteristic $0$, obtained in [M. Mackaay, V. Mazorchuk, V. Miemietz, D. Tubbenhauer and X. Zhang, Simple transitive $2$-representations of Soergel bimodules for finite Coxeter types. Proc. London Math. Soc. 126 (2023)].

papers.title: Cohomological and quasi-isometric diversity of groups with property $R_\infty$
papers.abstract: How rich is the collection of groups with a given prominent property? In this work we approach this question for property~$R_\infty$, which says that every automorphism $\varphi$ of a given group has infinitely many orbits under the $\varphi$-twisted conjugation action $(g,x) \mapsto gx\varphi(g)^{-1}$. Generalising the soluble groups of Herbert Abels to a large family over many integral domains, we prove that most such groups have property~$R_\infty$ drawing from a classical result of Levchuk and a swift observation by Jabara. Within the broad programme of cataloguing finitely generated groups up to quasi-isometry, our groups can then be separated by finiteness properties and cohomological dimension whilst having~$R_\infty$. Abandoning finite presentability, we establish that property~$R_\infty$ is very abundant in a strong sense: there are uncountably many finitely generated groups (which can all be chosen to be amenable or non-amenable) that have~$R_\infty$ and are pairwise not quasi-isometric. The proofs vary in flavour. On the amenable side we use carefully constructed quotients of Abels' groups and a general strategy for quasi-isometric diversity established by Minasyan, Osin, and Witzel. For the non-amenable constructions we rely on modifications of Leary's type $\mathtt{FP}$ groups, further cohomological arguments, and recent powerful criteria for~$R_\infty$ due to Iveson, Martino, Sgobbi, Wong, and Fournier-Facio.

papers.title: Cohomological change of coefficients for noncocommutative Hopf algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite Hopf algebra over a Noetherian commutative ring $R$. For any map $f : R \to k$ where $k$ is a field, there is a natural map on the cohomology of $A$ under this change of coefficients $H^\ast(f): H^\ast(A, R) \otimes_R k \to H^\ast(A_k, k)$. In this paper we examine this map for $R = \mathbb Z[\zeta]$ the cyclotomic integers with $\zeta$ an $\ell$th root of unity. We show that under a finite generation assumption, the induced map gives a homeomorphism on the spectra of the two cohomology rings. Finally, we turn to small quantum groups defined over $\mathbb Z[\zeta]$ and show that, with mild restrictions on $\ell$, every fiber map whose residue field has a good prime characteristic induces an isomorphism on cohomology.

papers.title: Collision Geometry and Holonomy of Finite Blaschke Model Spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate the rank-$n$ Hermitian vector bundle of finite Blaschke model spaces over the coefficient domain of monic polynomials whose zeros lie entirely in the open unit disk. By introducing a global anti-holomorphic rational frame, we show that both the bundle and its orthogonal-projection connection extend real-analytically across all internal root-collision strata. At the maximally coincident divisor, we compute the full curvature tensor explicitly; the successive differences of its matrix coefficients yield the standard matrix units, which implies that both the restricted and full holonomy groups coincide with the full unitary group $U(n)$. Furthermore, the induced metric on the determinant line bundle is shown to agree with the diagonal restriction of the Szegő kernel of the symmetrized polydisc, and its power-sum Kähler potential endows the coefficient domain with a complete Kähler metric. By contrast, once the Clark phase circle is adjoined to the base, the Clark spectral lines together with the canonical model-space conjugation single out a unique compatible unitary connection. This real-spectral connection is flat, extends real-analytically across internal collisions, and exhibits a finite signed cyclic holonomy group. We also derive a weighted residue formula for the complex-bilinear pairing induced by the canonical conjugation, and analyze explicit low-dimensional subfamilies that illustrate the sharp geometric contrast between the curved projection transport of the moving model space and the flat parallel transport of its real spectral lines.

papers.title: Comparing metric completions of triangulated categories with Verdier quotients
papers.abstract: Neeman's metric on a triangulated category assigns lengths to morphisms and allows us to construct triangulated metric completions of the category. We prove that the metric completion of a triangulated category with respect to a constant metric is always a subcategory of the Verdier quotient by the thick subcategory generated by cones of zero-length morphisms, and we provide a sufficient criterion for equality. To that end, we define continuous functors between completions which induce triangulated functors between completions. Moreover, we give two applications. First, we show that the additive equivalence discovered by Cummings and Gratz between the Paquette-Yildirim completion and a specific metric completion of an Igusa-Todorov discrete cluster category is, in fact, a triangulated equivalence. Second, we fully classify metric completions of bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves over weighted projective lines of domestic or tubular type.

papers.title: Comparison categories: the normal form and the regularity of comparison data
papers.abstract: There are many types of equivalence relations in mathematics, each one enjoying its own defnition, but many of them can also be defined by transformations of morphisms: Green's relations, orbit relations, conjugacy, equality of orbit closures, equivalence of Cauchy sequences, stable isomorphism. We unify them through the comparison category of a comparison datum, read at levels $-1,0,1,2,\dots$ (comparisons in both directions, connected components, homotopy groups). Its normal form is a full subcategory of a Grothendieck construction $\int_VH$ cut out by a map $s$; the classical relations are traced back to it by restriction along $s$, enrichment by a cost (limit relations) and filtered colimits (stabilization). If the map $\sigma$ transporting morphisms into a $2$-category is arbitrary, every relation occurs, so the constraint is the regularity of $\sigma$. We grade data along seven regularity classes. The rigid and diagonal classes are classified completely (on finite groups, by the double coset relations); completely functorial data contain conjugacy and obey a dichotomy on nil monoids. Whether every relation on a monoid is level $0$ of a completely functorial datum is open.

papers.title: Compatibility of Perverse Truncation of Ng\^o Fibrations
papers.abstract: We study compatibility of perverse truncations for morphisms between Ng\^o fibrations with rationally smooth total spaces. We show that, under an effective rank inequality, equivariant pullbacks preserve the normalized perverse truncations. Applied to the diagonal, this gives multiplicativity of perverse truncations for Hitchin systems with rationally smooth total spaces.

papers.title: Composition factors and finite representation type
papers.abstract: We prove that an Artin algebra has finite representation type if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture on composition factors and finite representation type recorded by Auslander, Reiten and Smalo.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Hironaka's Characteristic-$p$ Resolution: A Report On Queries to Frontier Agents
papers.abstract: Created on 23 October 2026, this manuscript draws on a frontier-dump investigation of Hironaka's proposed positive-characteristic resolution method. Taylor Dupuy initiated the queries during his talk How to Use AI in Mathematical Research Effectively at the University of Rochester Number Theory Seminar on that date. The findings were synthesized with harvest-dumps and developed into this manuscript with using-latexpowers. We examine the proposed positive-characteristic resolution mechanism of Hironaka (2017). Its negative-degree pieces are the unit ideal at a closed singular point where, for a common multiple $m$ of the generator degrees, $\wp(E,m)$ contains an element of order $m$. For the family $x^p+y^n$, with $n>2p$ and $p\nmid n$, the asserted transformation rule fails under the algebraic description of the characteristic algebra. With core focusing read by (44), the fixed local chain and the $\check E$ or $\hat E$ reading of the invariant, the length-one string agrees before and after the first blowup. With renewed chains and corresponding transported choices, the corresponding strings agree along the resolution sequence under either core-focusing reading. The two formulas for core focusing respectively retain the base-hiked exponent and, when its Inv-max stratum is smooth and closed, forget it. We give characteristic-$2$ limits on tail enclosure and a shade increase at a kangaroo point. These calculations do not supply a decreasing invariant or settle resolution. The mathematical draft of this manuscript was AI-generated by Claude Code from an AI-generated research record; its proofs received only AI review, and no human has checked them.

papers.title: Cowling’s conjecture: the almost connected case
papers.abstract: We prove that a locally compact group $G$ with amenable group $G/G^0$ of components has the Haagerup property if and only if it is weakly amenable with constant one. This proves Cowling's conjecture for connected Lie groups and almost connected locally compact groups. We also characterize weak amenability for arbitrary connected Lie groups and prove the product formula for the Cowling--Haagerup constant in terms of the simple factors of a Levi decomposition. Consequently, the constant is invariant under local isomorphism and decreases under quotients of connected locally compact groups. For groups with amenable group of components, it is unchanged by every closed central quotient. We deduce applications to lattices and their central quotients. The proof combines Ozawa's invariant-state obstruction with averaging over central characters and the tensor identity for induced representations.

papers.title: Criteria for a fiberwise Fujiki/Kahler family to be locally Moishezon/projective
papers.abstract: In this paper, we utilize the theory of non-K\"ahler loci by S. Boucksom to construct an integral $2$-cohomology class whose restriction to a general fiber is big, and then construct a relatively big line bundle via the exponential sequence. This leads to a local Moishezonness criterion for fibrations whose total spaces are compact complex manifolds in the Fujiki class $\mathscr{C}$, generalizing the bimeromorphic version of F. Campana's local projectivity theorem. We further combine a similar idea with the singular Demailly--P\u{a}un theorem by T. Collins--V. Tosatti to obtain a local projectivity criterion for fibrations from compact K\"ahler manifolds, yielding a new proof and a generalization of F. Campana's local projectivity theorem.

papers.title: Davenport constants with growing binary rank
papers.abstract: We study the correction to the standard lower bound $D^*$ for Davenport constants of finite abelian groups with a growing elementary two-component. For every fixed nontrivial abelian $p$-group $H$ of odd order, we prove $D(H\oplus C_2^r)=D^*(H\oplus C_2^r)+(D(H)-1)\log_2 r+O_H(1)$, with a uniform version for varying $H$. For $C_3\oplus C_2^r$, we determine exact values on explicit infinite intervals of ranks. More generally, the correction is logarithmic or smaller precisely when the fixed group has at most one odd prime divisor. We show that the two-primary part affects the logarithmic coefficient: for $C_{24}\oplus C_2^r$, the ratio $(D-D^*)/\log_2 r$ has limsup at least $2.4933231\ldots>2$, whereas for $C_3\oplus C_2^r$ the limit is $2$. These upper limiting coefficients are unbounded even with the odd prime fixed. The proofs use binary codes and finite-field Fourier analysis.

papers.title: Degenerate complex structures on surfaces and stability conditions
papers.abstract: Physical heuristics suggest that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions of a projective Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ should be related to the moduli space of complex structures on its mirror $X^\vee$. On the other hand, recent work in the literature introduces a modular partial compactification, $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$, of a quotient of the space of stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}^{b}(X)$. We provide some mathematical evidence for the aforementioned heuristics by proving that for curves and surfaces, certain boundary strata in $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ describe degenerate complex structures on $X^\vee$.
