Along the way, we introduce a criterion for producing boundary points of $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ when $\mathcal{D}$ is an arbitrary $k$-linear triangulated category. As a byproduct, we deduce the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on certain quotients of the derived categories of K3 and Enriques surfaces.

papers.title: Degeneration of (-1)-shifted symplectic stacks and categorification of Donaldson-Thomas invariants
papers.abstract: We study cohomological Donaldson-Thomas invariants of perfect complexes in a semistable degeneration of projective Calabi-Yau threefolds, with smooth components $X_1,X_2$ meeting along a smooth anticanonical surface $S$. The generic fiber of degeneration family is a $(-1)$-shifted symplectic stack. Over the special fiber, the derived restriction to $S$ is derived Lagrangian, and its homotopy fiber product is also $(-1)$-shifted symplectic. Our goal is to relate the categorical DT invariants of the generic fiber moduli, induced by periodic cyclic homology of matrix factorization category of 0-shifted potential functions over such moduli, to that of the special fiber obtained via derived Lagrangian intersection and geometric quantization. This is achieved via construction of a flat Gauss-Manin connection that relates the generic fiber cohomological DT invariants to that of the special fiber. The geometric framework, universal trace diagrams, and fourfold foliation were developed jointly with Jacob Kryczka in arXiv:2510.20325. Here we construct ordinary critical realizations, oriented cyclic-to-bar comparisons, and Gauss-Manin operators, and verify finite specialization in explicit moduli problems. We workout our construction via several explicit examples such as Grassmannians, Relative Hilbert Schemes and moduli space of pure 2 dimensional sheaves with support moving in a fixed linear system of divisors in the ambient threefold.

papers.title: Diagrams for Roots and Quiver Representations in the context of the Gabriel-Kac Theorem
papers.abstract: Using the data of the Dynkin diagrams, we build graphical calculi for representing the positive roots of Kac-Moody algebras and the representations of quivers. Once developed, we use these to analyze the asymptotic size of the root and representation spaces, and discuss how this relates to the Gabriel-Kac theorem, the correspondence between these two structures. We give a refinement of this correspondence in terms of the trichotomy of growth rates for Kac-Moody algebras depending on if they are of finite, affine, or indefinite type, which is done in terms of what we call ``tree like" representations.

papers.title: Diamonds: Homology and the Central Series of Groups
papers.abstract: We establish an analog of a theorem of Stallings which asserts the homomorphisms between the universal nilpotent quotients induced by a homomorphism $G \to H$ of groups are isomorphisms provided a pair of homological conditions are satisfied. Our analogy does not have a homomorphism between $G$ and $H$ but instead $G,H \leq G_0$ that satisfies a similar homological condition. We derive a few applications of this result. First, we show that there exist pairs of non-isomorphic number fields whose absolute Galois groups have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. We show that there exists pairs of non-isometric hyperbolic $n$-manifolds whose fundamental groups are residually nilpotent and have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. These are the first examples of residually nilpotent Kleinian groups with arbitrarily large nilpotent genus. Complex hyperbolic 2-manifold examples are given as well. Considering Riemann surfaces and complex hyperbolic 2-manifolds as projective curves and surfaces defined over a number field, we show the (outer) action of the absolute Galois group of the field of definition on the universal nilpotent quotients of the geometric fundamental groups are equivalent. This is in contrast to fact that the (outer) Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve determines the curve by work of Mochizuki. In particular, the nilpotent representation theory of the geometric fundamental group is not anabelian.

papers.title: Dimensions of Fano schemes of lines on hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbb{C}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$. We prove that an $m$-dimensional integral projective family of lines sweeping a variety of dimension $y$ satisfies $m\le\max\{2y-d-1,n-3\}$. This proves the de Jong-Debarre conjecture for $d\le n$ and the Beheshti-Starr bound for lines on smooth hypersurfaces for $d\ge n+1$.

papers.title: Dynamical systems as enriched functors
papers.abstract: This article presents a general description of dynamical systems using the language of enriched functors and enriched natural transformations. This framework is essential to establish the equivalence of three descriptions of dynamics -- a semigroup action on the domain; a parameterized family of endomorphisms; and a transformation of time-space into the collection of endomorphisms. A collection of categorical axioms are presented that provides a complete categorical language to develop dynamical systems theory. None of the assumptions are rooted in specific contexts such as topology and measure spaces. The equivalence of the three descriptions is further used to construct other related notions,such as transfer operators, orbits and shift-spaces. All of these objects are defined by their structural role and universal properties, instead of their usual pointwise definitions.

papers.title: Enumeration of plane unicuspidal curves of any genus via tropical geometry
papers.abstract: We enumerate complex curves on toric surfaces of any given degree and genus, having a single cusp and nodes as their singularities, and matching appropriately many point constraints. The solution is obtained via tropical enumerative geometry. The same technique applies to enumeration of real plane cuspidal curves: We show that, for any fixed $r\ge1$ and $d\ge2r+3$, there exists a generic real $2r$-dimensional linear family of plane curves of degree $d$ in which the number of real $r$-cuspidal curves is asymptotically comparable with the total number of complex $r$-cuspidal curves in the family, as $d\to\infty$.

papers.title: Equivalence of freeness and higher order freeness of hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: Using vector bundle theory, we prove that an essential hyperplane arrangement in an $\ell$-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero is free if and only if its module of logarithmic derivations of order $p$ is free for some $1\le p\le\ell-1$. The same statement holds for multiarrangements.

papers.title: Essential $p$-dimension and Chern numbers
papers.abstract:
Let $X$ be a smooth, projective, connected variety over a field $k$ containing a root of unity of order $p$. If $X$ has a Chern number prime to $p$, we show that every finite $p$-group acting on $X$ acts through a subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_n(k)$, where $n=\dim X$. This allows one to transfer properties of representations of finite $p$-groups to their actions on $X$. We deduce a fixed-point theorem which, unlike earlier results of this kind, is sensitive to the arithmetic of the base field, and whose dimensional bound is sharp for each individual group (apart from one low-dimensional case when $p=2$). We also obtain restrictions on finite $p$-groups of birational automorphisms of rationally connected varieties; for instance the Cremona group $\operatorname{Cr}_n(\mathbb{Q})$ contains no element of order $p^2$ when $p \ge n+2$.
  More generally, we prove variants of these results in the presence of a Chern number not divisible by a given power of $p$.
  The method is based on the following observation about the essential $p$-dimension $\operatorname{ed}_p(G)$ of an affine algebraic group $G$: over a field of characteristic zero, the number $\operatorname{ed}_p(G) + \dim G$ is the least dimension of a smooth projective variety $Y$ with a generically free $G$-action such that the degree map $\operatorname{CH}_G(Y) \to \mathbb{F}_p$ from the equivariant Chow group is nonzero. The Chern numbers modulo $p$ of $Y$ lie in the image of this map; combined with Karpenko and Merkurjev's computation of the essential $p$-dimension of finite $p$-groups, this yields our results.

papers.title: Examples of rigid Twistor D-modules
papers.abstract: The well-established theory of D-modules gives a framework to study linear differential equations from the perspective of algebraic geometry. A significant advancement in this theory has been the introduction of Twistor D-modules by Claude Sabbah and Takuro Mochizuki: These objects expose inherent, but hidden information of the underlying differential equations in an elegant way. We explain the foundational concepts of Twistor D-modules and give concrete examples of these objects. We introduce a notion of rigidity for Twistor D-modules, which these examples fulfill. We conclude with a certain algebraicity conjecture about rigid Twistor D-modules, which we prove in a special case.

papers.title: Existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for weighted complete intersections
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth well formed Fano or Calabi-Yau weighted complete intersection admits a nef-partition. As an application, we establish the existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for all such Fano weighted complete intersections.

papers.title: Extending Upper Cluster Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be an upper cluster algebra, which is a subalgebra of $R$. Suppose that there is some cluster variable $x_e$ such that ${R}_{{x}_e} = S[{x}_e^{\pm 1}]$. We try to understand under which conditions ${R}$ is an upper cluster algebra, and how the quiver of $R$ relates to that of $S$. Moreover, if the restriction of $(\Delta,W)$ to some subquiver is a cluster model, we give a sufficient condition for $(\Delta,W)$ itself being a cluster model. As an application, we show that the semi-invariant ring of any complete $m$-tuple flags is an upper cluster algebra whose quiver is explicitly given. Moreover, the quiver with its rigid potential is a polyhedral cluster model.

papers.title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
papers.abstract: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.

papers.title: Finite-rank rigidity and Nash-curve discreteness for correlation potentials
papers.abstract: For every nonconstant real polynomial P of degree k and every positive rational exponent a/b, minimizing the spherical energy with potential |P(t)|^{a/b} admits a discrete solution with at most $\binom{d+2ak-1}{2ak}+\binom{d+2ak-2}{2ak-1}$ support points, where a/b is reduced. This finite-replacement consequence needs no denominator threshold. Under a multiplicity-sensitive denominator condition, we prove the stronger conclusion that every minimizer has an explicit uniform support bound; suitable negative positive-semidefinite perturbations preserve that bound. We present these consequences before the machinery. The main arguments simplify irrational-power finite-rank rigidity and give a Nash-curve ramification obstruction, stable under entire scalar additions, for powers, logarithms, and rational poles. The latter yields uniform finite supports on compact semialgebraic curves without assuming that the supports are semialgebraic. The known p-frame finite-replacement principle is distinguished from the extensions developed here. No unconditional discreteness theorem for general irrational p is claimed.

papers.title: Fourier-Mukai partners of abelian varieties and K3 surfaces in positive and mixed characteristics
papers.abstract: We study Fourier-Mukai equivalences of (families of) abelian varieties and K3 surfaces in positive and mixed characteristics. We first prove in any characteristics that Fourier-Mukai partners of abelian varieties are again abelian varieties. We subsequently focus on the canonical lifts of ordinary abelian varieties and ordinary K3 surfaces. For such schemes, we show that Fourier-Mukai equivalences on the special fibers can be lifted to the canonical lifts. We also prove that the relative Fourier-Mukai partners of the canonical lifts are in bijection with the Fourier-Mukai partners of the special fibers. We conclude by demonstrating that the last result can be used to recover the ordinary case of a result originally proved by Honigs, Lombardi and Tirabassi.

papers.title: Frobenius kernels of algebraic supergroups and Steinberg's tensor product theorem
papers.abstract: For a split quasireductive supergroup $G$ defined over a field, we study structure and representation of Frobenius kernels $G_r$ of $G$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for $G_r$ to be unimodular in terms of the root system of $G$. We also establish Steinberg's tensor product theorem for $G$ under some natural assumptions.

papers.title: Galois module structure of Deligne--Lusztig varieties for $\mathrm{GL}_3$
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)\to\overline{\mathbf{X}}(w)$ be the ramified Galois cover of compactified Deligne--Lusztig varieties. Our objects of study are the Lefschetz numbers for the action of the finite covering group $T^{wF}$ on the coherent cohomology of the structure sheaf of $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$. The Lefschetz numbers for all elements of $T^{wF}$ determine the virtual $T^{wF}$-representation given by the alternating sum of these cohomology groups. In the two cases of Deligne--Lusztig surfaces of type $A_2$ and ${}^{2}A_2$, we give explicit formulas for the Lefschetz numbers for a generator of the stabilizer of an irreducible component. It follows that the equivariant Euler characteristic of the compactification $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$ is not virtually free as a virtual module over the covering group.

papers.title: Generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and unirationality of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $2$
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and study their relation to quasi-\'etale double covers. As an application, we prove that a del Pezzo surface of degree $2$ over an infinite field of characteristic different from $2$ is unirational if it has a rational generalized Eckardt point. This resolves a previously open case not covered by Manin's construction.

papers.title: Geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack
papers.abstract: The analytic Emerton-Gee stack is a rigid analytic moduli stack of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules over the Robba ring, and is expected to play a fundamental role in the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for locally analytic representations. In this paper, we establish the fundamental geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack: it is a rigid analytic Artin stack, normal, a local complete intersection, and equidimensional of the expected dimension. As an application, our normality result removes the reducedness hypothesis in the paper of Le, Strauch, and Wang, thereby yielding an unconditional proof of the conjecture on the global sections of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack formulated by Emerton, Gee, and Hellmann.

papers.title: Geometry of $m$-direct-sum morphisms
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a complex vector space of dimension $mk$ ($m\ge2$). A morphism from a positive-dimensional projective variety $f\colon X\to\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$ is $m$-direct-sum if $V=U_{x_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus U_{x_m}$ for every $m$ pairwise distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_m$ on $X$, where $U_x\subset V$ is the subspace represented by $f(x)$. We show that $X$ is necessarily a smooth rational curve. When the so-called drill $d(f)$ of $f$ is $1$ or when the rank $k$ is at most $2$, we give complete classifications of $f$ up to the automorphisms of $\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$. As applications, we classify all so-called skew scrolls in $\mathbb{P}^3$, which completely answers a question of Day. Then we show that if $X\subset \mathbb{P}(V)$ is a smooth, projective, nondegenerate subvariety whose higher-order Terracini locus is empty, then $X$ is the rational normal curve, which strengthens the critical Terracini rigidity discovered by Ballico and Chiantini. By using the same machinery, we also prove a dual version of Terracini rigidity. Finally, we show that $m$-unisolvent systems form an abelian category of finite length and that $7$ is the least diagonal exponent of a simple rank-three $2$-unisolvent system.

papers.title: GKM Theory for Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices in Lie Type D
papers.abstract: We study the manifold $Q_{\G, \lambda}$ of isospectral real skew-symmetric matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern determined by a graph $\G$. The compact torus $T^n$ acts naturally on $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ by conjugation, and this action can be studied using GKM theory. We prove two results about this manifold and its GKM graph. The first theorem describes how the GKM graph of $Q_{\G, \lambda}$ is obtained from the GKM graph of the corresponding manifold $M_{\G, \lambda}$ of isospectral Hermitian matrices. The second theorem shows that equivariant formality of $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ implies equivariant formality of $M_{\Gamma,\lambda}$, whereas the converse fails.

papers.title: Graftings and cograftings for species
papers.abstract: We introduce graftings and cograftings for vector species, modelled on the elementary operations of adjoining and deleting a root in a rooted forest. We relate these maps to operads, up and down operators, and obtain nontrivial balanced pairs, admitting pair of creation/annihilation operators with commuting relations. We establish universal properties for the species of rooted forests. Using Fock functors, we recover the classical Connes--Kreimer Hopf algebra, its noncommutative planar analogue, and Foissy's $q$-infinitesimal Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics on nilpotent Lie groups and the quasicentroid condition
papers.abstract: We study left-invariant Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics (cyclic-parallel Ricci tensor) on nilpotent Lie groups, focusing on the algebraic condition that the Ricci operator belongs to the quasicentroid $\operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}$. We review and develop the abstract structure theory of quasicentroids, and prove a Central Decomposition Theorem: any nilpotent Riemannian Lie algebra with $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ decomposes as a central product of ideals $\mathfrak{i}_j = E_{\lambda_j} \oplus \mathfrak{z}$, where $\mathfrak{z}$ is the center of $\mathfrak{n}$ and $E_{\lambda_j}$ are the negative Ricci eigenspaces. Endowed with the restricted metric, each factor $\mathfrak{i}_j$ is itself a Gray $\mathcal{A}$-space. Finally, we investigate when the general $\mathcal{A}$-metric condition reduces to $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$. We prove this equivalence unconditionally for two-step nilpotent algebras and whenever the metric admits a nice basis, and provide a general characterization via the vanishing of two trace identities.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten Generating Series of Elliptic Curves and Iterated Integrals of Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
papers.abstract: We compute various types of iterated integrals of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms that are constructed from the Kronecker theta function. Furthermore, we relate the generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves to these iterated integrals.

papers.title: Harmonic Analysis on $p$-adic Unipotent Groups
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $\chi$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$.
  To the character $\chi$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_\chi=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $\chi$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition
  of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_\chi$. We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition. As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.

papers.title: Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface. Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve. Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is constant in linear series on K3 surfaces.

papers.title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected K\"ahler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.

papers.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
papers.abstract:
Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive.
  The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$.
  We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.

papers.title: Hyperstructures as complete atomic Boolean algebras
papers.abstract: We show that several categories of hyperstructures, including the mosaics of Nakamura and Reyes and the hypergroups of Marty, are realizable as categories of objects with extra structure within the category of complete atomic Boolean algebras (CABAs) and atom-preserving morphisms.

papers.title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.

papers.title: Infinite divisibility of hitting times for symmetric stable processes
papers.abstract: Let \(T_a\) be the first hitting time of a nonzero point \(a\) by a symmetric strictly \(\alpha\)-stable L\'evy process, where \(1<\alpha<2\). We give a computer-assisted classification of its ordinary additive infinite divisibility. There is a unique threshold \(\alpha_*\), with \(1.6670659903<\alpha_*<1.6670659915\), such that \(T_a\) is infinitely divisible if and only if \(1<\alpha\le\alpha_*\). The threshold is characterized by a unique zero contact of the canonical inverse logarithmic-derivative kernel. The proof combines explicit analytic estimates, rigorous interval covers, Gaussian necessary conditions and Rouch\'e's theorem. In particular, a fully analytic argument proves failure of infinite divisibility for every \(15/8\le\alpha<2\). Scalar bounds at the two time ends reduce the compact interval computations. The finite computations and their acceptance conditions are supplied as ancillary material.

papers.title: Integral crystalline Tate classes of codimension two at supersingular points of Mumford's fourfolds
papers.abstract: For a supersingular abelian variety $X$ over $\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p$, let $T^4(X)$ be the lattice of integral crystalline Tate classes of codimension $2$ and $S(X)$ the span of products of divisor classes. Let $p\ge5$ and $\mathscr{G}_p$ be the $p$-divisible group of the supersingular points of Mumford's families of abelian fourfolds at primes inert in their cubic field, for the hyperspecial levels given by tensor-induced lattices. For every abelian fourfold $X$ with $X[p^\infty]\cong\mathscr{G}_p$ we show that $T^4(X)/S(X)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/p)^4$, and that the integral crystalline Tate conjecture holds in codimension $2$ on $X$ if statements in a preprint of Markman hold. At these primes, Kisin's crystalline tensors make the Dieudonné module a tensor product of three rank-$2$ modules permuted cyclically by Frobenius, and at supersingular points Frobenius maps a tensor basis to multiples of basis vectors. For such monomial modules all lattices involved are spanned by multiples of basis vectors, with exponents given by min-plus formulas independent of $p$. Under the endomorphisms, $T^4/S$ is a non-split extension of $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^2$ by $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^2$, generated by one Weil class of an inert imaginary quadratic action. Assuming these statements, an algebraic such class comes from specializing a Weil cycle on a fourfold with complex multiplication. A projector that is a polynomial in an endomorphism, and an intersection matrix with unit determinant, fix its $p$-adic normalization without a comparison theorem. At unramified non-inert primes with such levels, $T^4=S$ at the supersingular points. Of the fourteen isomorphism classes of monomial supersingular Dieudonné modules of height $8$, the conjecture holds unconditionally for nine, under the same assumption for that of $\mathscr{G}_p$, and is open for four. The indices are computed exactly with integers.

papers.title: Intrinsic Non-Reductive Geometric Invariant Theory and Moduli Spaces of Principal Bundles with Non-Reductive Structure Groups
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of moduli spaces for algebraic stacks with a weak action of $\Theta = [\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m]$ (including stacks of filtered objects and unstable $\Theta$-strata) for which the center admits a good moduli space and the retraction to the center has flat, finitely presented relative inertia, providing a stack-intrinsic generalization of the existence of non-reductive Geometric Invariant Theory quotients. As an application, we construct quasi-projective coarse moduli spaces of principal bundles over a smooth projective curve with non-reductive structure groups, including moduli spaces of Ramanathan unstable principal bundles of fixed Harder--Narasimhan type.

papers.title: K\"ahler-Einstein toric submanifolds of the projective space
papers.abstract: We show that the K\"ahler-Einstein metrics on the four families of symmetric toric Fano manifolds due to Batyrev and Selivanova cannot be induced by immersions into projective spaces equipped with the Fubini-Study metric. We also show a similar conclusion for the non-symmetric examples discovered by Nill and Paffenholz. As an application we obtain that a centrally symmetric toric Fano manifold admits a K\"ahler-Einstein metric induced by a projective immersion if and only if it is a product of projective lines. These results confirm for each of these examples a broader conjecture characterizing the K\"ahler--Einstein metrics that can be induced by projective immersions.

papers.title: Laurent and g-vector counterexamples for quivers with homotopies
papers.abstract: We give negative answers to the general Laurent-phenomenon question and the g-vector sign-coherence question for quivers with homotopies posed by Li, Liu, Mou and Pan.

papers.title: Lie (super)algebras generated by reflections in finite reflection groups of exceptional type
papers.abstract: Using a mixture of theoretical tools and computer calculations, we describe the Lie subalgebras and the Lie sub-superalgebras generated by the sets of reflections in the group algebras of the exceptional finite reflection groups.

papers.title: Local wild mapping class groups and cabled braids
papers.abstract: We will define and study some generalisations of pure $\mathfrak{g}$-braid groups that occur in the theory of connections on curves, for any complex reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. They make up local pieces of the wild mapping class groups, which are fundamental groups of (universal) deformations of wild Riemann surfaces, underlying the braiding of Stokes data and generalising the usual mapping class groups. We will establish a general product decomposition for the local wild mapping class groups, and in many cases define a fission tree controlling this decomposition. Further in type A we will show one obtains cabled versions of braid groups, related to braid operads.

papers.title: Logarithmic transformations on the six-sphere
papers.abstract: We show that there are infinitely many choices of the multiplicities in the logarithmic transformation step of the Alp\"oge--Claude construction which produce a complex threefold diffeomorphic to the six-sphere. Moreover, distinct choices of the multiplicities yield biholomorphically inequivalent complex structures.

papers.title: Maximal Curves with Few Automorphisms
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of constructing maximal curves with few automorphisms over finite fields. Our main ingredient is the determination of the \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\!\left(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\right)\)-stabilizer of the roots of the Chebyshev polynomials, apart from two exceptional cases already treated in the literature. We prove that, in all other cases, the only nontrivial M\"obius symmetry is the sign involution. This settles the general case for the automorphism groups of the corresponding Chebyshev curves. We further construct an infinite family of maximal curves of unbounded genus whose only nontrivial automorphism is the hyperelliptic involution. This reveals a contrasting phenomenon to the common heuristic that curves with many rational points tend to have large automorphism groups.

papers.title: Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally
papers.abstract: We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold. We discuss how to define symmetrizers, hyperbolizations, and constraints for minimally coupled natural equations, and we show how these can be used to recover standard existence and uniqueness results, relative to any choice of background structure (a metric, for minimally coupled systems). Additionally, we show that minimal coupling and naturality together imply that the causal cones associated with a (first order, quasilinear, minimally coupled) naturally symmetric hyperbolic natural equation must always coincide with the metric lightcones, and that a certain rank-2 tensor, associates with a natural hyperbolization, must always be divergence free relative to the associated Levi-Civita derivative operator.

papers.title: Moduli space of irregular singular $\lambda$-connections and the relative symplectic form
papers.abstract: We study the moduli space of $\lambda$-connections with ramified singularities on a smooth projective curve $X$. We construct a quasi-projective relative moduli scheme $M^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Hod}} \to \Lambda$ of $\alpha$-stable $\lambda$-connections over a base parameter space $\Lambda$. This moduli space connects the irregular de Rham moduli space ($\lambda=1$) and the irregular Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs bundles equipped with non-zero irregular local exponents ($\lambda=0$). Furthermore, we show that $M^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Hod}}$ is smooth over $\Lambda$ and carries a canonical relative symplectic form $\omega_{M^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Hod}}/\Lambda}$, yielding a natural Poisson structure on the total space.

papers.title: Moment Polyptychs and the Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric variety of complex dimension $2n$ using symplectic cutting. When the defining arrangement is cooriented so that its base region is non-empty and bounded, fibre rotation has proper moment map and produces compact K\"ahler orbifold cuts carrying the residual torus action. We introduce the moment polyptych of such a cut, a polytopal complex assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and show that its vertices and local lattice data determine the fixed points, tangent weights, and finite orbifold groups required for equivariant orbifold Riemann-Roch localisation. Even for a smooth hypertoric manifold, a reducible core forces every cut in the outer cut chamber to have non-trivial cyclic isotropy, while the cuts are smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety, which is then a product of projective spaces. For a positive regular integral level $d$ in the outer cut chamber, algebraic cutting identifies the cut's quantisation with a finite filtration piece of the circle-graded quantisation of the original hypertoric variety, whose successive quotients recover the individual circle-weight spaces. We prove that the higher cohomology of the pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes at every such level, so that the localised index is the character of the actual space of sections. Finally, a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is the arrangement slack function, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. Thus, each finite stage admits a weighted lattice-point description whose multiplicity function is supported on the lattice points in the support of the level-$d$ moment polyptych.

papers.title: Monoidal structures on triangulated fibered categories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a small category admitting binary products. There exists a canonical dictionary expressing the structure and properties of monoidal $\mathcal{S}$-fibered categories in terms of the external tensor product in place of the usual internal tensor product. In this paper, we specialize this dictionary to the setting of triangulated $\mathcal{S}$-fibered categories, by studying how the general translation process interacts with shift functors. Our results provide a satisfactory abstract framework to study monoidal structures from the perspective of perverse sheaves.

papers.title: Near-Null Limits and Contact Distributions for Maxwell Composite Operators
papers.abstract: We investigate the simultaneous near-null, longitudinal-continuum, and ultraviolet limits of four-point correlation functions of quadratic composite operators in Maxwell theory. Taking the external momenta to be collinear and spacelike, we weight each loop integral by a smooth test function of the routed longitudinal momentum. All three connected Wick contraction cycles are generated from a common Gaussian source functional and regulated by a cutoff on the total proper time. For the resulting integrals restricted to a fixed ultraviolet proper-time interval, we establish the uniform bound $\left|\mathcal I_{\delta,M}^{\epsilon}[\phi]-\mathcal I_{0,\infty}^{\epsilon}[\phi]\right|\le C\|\phi\|_{C_b^8}\left(\delta\epsilon^{-3}+M^{-2}\delta^{-3}\epsilon^{-1}\right)$, where $\delta$ denotes the dimensionless near-null tilt parameter and $M$ specifies the longitudinal lattice resolution. This estimate determines the joint scaling regimes under which a universal counterterm subtraction yields an identical renormalized finite part. We further show that the longitudinal logarithmic divergence of the alternating chiral cycle is governed by the measure $8\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}\mathrm d\xi+3\delta_0+3\delta_1$, whereas each of the other two cycles contributes $8\mathbf 1_{(0,2)}\mathrm d\xi$. These distributional coefficients emerge from the complete covariant numerators, including the instantaneous longitudinal terms. Finally, for the alternating cycle and any smooth compactly supported test function coinciding with $\xi^2$ in a neighborhood of $[0,1]$, the critical trajectory $\delta=c\epsilon^3$ with $M^2\delta^3\epsilon\to\infty$ leaves a finite discrepancy of $30c$, demonstrating the sharpness of the tilt scaling. The proof combines exact Gaussian moment reductions, whole-line quadrature error bounds, and an explicit evaluation of boundary jets.

papers.title: Nevanlinna Theory on Berkovich Curves
papers.abstract: We develop a value distribution theory for finite analytic morphisms between proper connected quasi-smooth Berkovich curves over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. The central tool is a multi-tail Dirichlet Green function on finite truncations of a generalized skeleton, which makes non-Archimedean potential theory on skeleta compatible with global Nevanlinna asymptotics. Using it, we prove the first main theorem as an exact identity relating the characteristic, counting, and proximity functions. For logarithmic targets we establish a second main theorem in both ramified and level-one truncated forms. The defect relation is also given. The theory provides a Berkovich-analytic framework for non-Archimedean value distribution, bridging classical Nevanlinna theory and its $p$-adic counterpart.

papers.title: Nijenhuis Lie $n$-algebras
papers.abstract:
We introduce a homotopical framework for Nijenhuis operators on semistrict Lie $n$-algebras ($n$-term $L_\infty$-algebras) for every $n \ge 1$ and, more generally, on arbitrary $L_\infty$-algebras. A Nijenhuis operator is defined as a family $N = (N_q)_{q \ge 1}$ of multilinear maps, with $N_1$ linear, realizing an $L_\infty$-morphism from an $N$-twisted copy of the structure to the original one. We prove that this condition is equivalent to the vanishing, at every arity $m$, of the $m$-th Nijenhuis torsion up to a correction term $\Lambda^N_m$ formed by higher-component substitutions, and we provide a closed combinatorial formula for $\Lambda^N_m$ as a sum over set partitions. Along the way, we show that the arity-$k$ Nijenhuis torsion factors canonically as a composite of $k$ commuting elementary slot deformations.
  The resulting objects form a category $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$; we establish that $\mathbf{NijLie}_m$ embeds as the full subcategory of $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$ on objects concentrated in the bottom
  $m$ degrees for all $m \le n$. These levels assemble into a tower whose first three stages are classical Nijenhuis Lie algebras, the Nijenhuis Lie $2$-algebras of Das, and the newly introduced Nijenhuis Lie $3$-algebras. We characterize the strict and skeletal objects at every level, introduce $n$-term representations up to homotopy of a Nijenhuis Lie algebra,
  and prove that the semidirect product construction establishes an equivalence between the category of such representations and split abelian $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$-extensions.
  Finally, two corrections to published level-three identities are documented, and all component identities up to arity five are verified via computer algebra.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean John, Non-Archimedean Dvoretzky-Milman, Non-Archimedean Type-Cotype and Non-Archimedean Kwapien Problems
papers.abstract: We ask for non-Archimedean version of following four: (1) John Theorem, (2) Dvoretzky-Milman Theorem, (3) Type-Cotype of Banach space, (4) Kwapien Theorem.

papers.title: Non-linear contexts and dependent operads
papers.abstract: We study the category $\mathbf{Dep_{aff}}$ of finite posets and opfibrations between them, and prove that it is a perfect operator category in the sense of Barwick. Based on its additional properties, we propose a definition for a dependent operator category, and formulate a notion of dependent affine operad in a fibered way. In the particular case of $\mathbf{Dep_{aff}}$, we investigate the basic theory of such operads, establishing that the category of algebras for an operad is monadic over a canonical presheaf topos of "dependent sets". We finally extend this theory to a setting where we allow variable duplication, which we refer to as general dependent operads.

papers.title: Normal Functions, Even Theta Characteristics and the Theta Divisor
papers.abstract: Let $[C]$ be a point in the moduli space of curves $\mathcal{M}_g$, with $g>1$, lying outside a countable union of closed nowhere--dense subsets of an analytic parameter space for $\mathcal M_g$. Let $G \,\subset\, J(C)$ be a connected compact subgroup of real dimension $1$ of the Jacobian of $C$, and let $L$ be an even theta characteristic on $C$. We prove that $\{\zeta \, \in\, G\ \big\vert\,\ H^0(C,\, L \otimes \zeta)\,\not=\, 0 \}\, =\, \emptyset$ if and only if $L \otimes \zeta_G$ is an even theta characteristic on $C$, where $\zeta_G$ is the unique non-trivial point of $G$ of order two.

papers.title: Notes on the Kuznetsov component of cubic sevenfolds
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a cubic 7-fold. When $Y$ is smooth, its Kuznetsov component is a Calabi-Yau category of dimension 3, and we construct an embedding of the Kuznetsov component into the derived category of Clifford modules over $\mathbb{P}^4$. When $Y$ is a general cubic 7-fold singular along a line, we construct an explicit weakly crepant categorical resolution of its Kuznetsov component by the derived category of a smooth Calabi-Yau 3-fold, recovering a result of Favero-Kelly. In this construction, we express the resolution functor explicitly as a composition of geometric functors and mutations, and identify its kernel with a category equivalent to a pull-back of the derived category of a stacky curve.

papers.title: Obstructions to embedding singular curves in toric varieties
papers.abstract: For every integer $d \geq 2$, we show that there exists an irreducible, reduced curve which embeds in $\mathbb{P}^d$ but in no projective normal toric variety of dimension less than $d$. In particular, there exist reduced irreducible curves that embed in $\mathbb{P}^d$ but do not embed in any weighted projective space of dimension less than $d$.

papers.title: On Lin's Arithmetic–Geometric Means Conjecture for Singular Values
papers.abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be positive semidefinite, and let $0\le t\le 1$. Lin (2017) conjectured that $\lambda_j((1-t)A+tB)\ge\sigma_j^{1/2}(A^{2(1-t)}B^{2t})$ for $j=1,\ldots,n$. The case $t=1/2$ is Drury's theorem, which answered a long-standing question of Bhatia and Kittaneh. Lin remarked that Drury's method does not seem to reach other values of $t$. We prove his conjecture for every $t\in[0,1]$. The proof builds on Drury's argument, but replaces his block-matrix step (unique to the midpoint $t=1/2$) by an eigenvalue count based on an inertia identity and a one-variable inequality.

papers.title: On stable twist 2-groups of quasi-Hopf algebras
papers.abstract:
For any finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebra $A$, we define the notion of a stable twist of $A$. We show that stable twists form a strict 2-group $\2ust(A)$, which is equivalent to $\OAut(\C{A})^{\rev}$. Given a group homomorphism $\rho: G \to \ost(A)$, we determine the obstruction in $H^3(G,Z_G(A))$ to lift $\rho$ to a $G$-action on $\C{A}$. We also establish a bijection between such liftings and cocentral cleft extensions of $\k[G]$ by $A$.
  The main application of $\2ust(A)$ is the computation of $\OAut(\C{A})$, together with an explicit description of the corresponding tensor autoequivalences. We apply this framework to pointed Hopf algebras $A$ that arise as central extensions of Taft algebras by cyclic groups, and we explicitly determine all of their tensor autoequivalences. The equivariantizations of $\C{A}$ by $\ost(A)$ produce a new family of Hopf algebras $\N(n,\xi)$ of dimension $2nm$, where $\xi$ is a scalar of order $m\mid n$ such that neither $\N(n,\xi)$ nor its dual has the Chevalley property.
  In dimension 24, we prove that $\N(6,-1)$ and its dual are precisely the Hopf algebras $H$ for which neither $H$ nor $H^*$ has the Chevalley property. This completes the classification of nonsemisimple Hopf algebras of dimension 24.

papers.title: On Terao's conjecture for at most nine planes
papers.abstract: In this note we show that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of at most nine planes in the complex projective $3$-space. Moreover, we show that every essential and irreducible free arrangement of at most nine planes in $\mathbb{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is divisionally free, and we list all intersection lattices of such arrangements. Our approach is based on Ziegler's restriction theorem and a simple count involving the numbers of multiple lines. As a by-product, we show that Cynk--Szemberg octic arrangements are never free. Finally, motivated by a recent work of Dimca and Pokora, we present examples of weak Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements, including pairs of octic arrangements leading to rigid double octic Calabi--Yau threefolds.

papers.title: On the Blasius-Deligne conjecture for the standard $L$-functions of symplectic type
papers.abstract: The Blasius-Deligne conjecture for automorphic $L$-functions is about the period relations and the algebraicity of critical $L$-values. In this paper, we prove the Blasius-Deligne conjecture for standard $L$-functions attached to regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of $GL_{2n}$ of symplectic type, under the expected Galois invariance condition for these representations. The main results extend the classical work of G. Shimura and Y. Manin from $GL_2$ to $GL_{2n}$, and complete the approach that was initially taken by H. Grobner and A. Raghuram and by F. Januszewski, where a few technical assumptions were taken.

papers.title: On the decomposition group of a nonsingular plane cubic by a log Calabi-Yau geometrical perspective
papers.abstract: This paper aims to study the decomposition group of a nonsingular plane cubic under the light of the log Calabi-Yau geometry. Using this approach we prove that an appropriate algorithm of the Sarkisov program in dimension 2 applied to an element of this group is automatically volume preserving. From this, we deduce some properties of the (volume preserving) Sarkisov factorization of its elements. We also confirm an expectation by Blanc, Pan and Vust on the splitting property of the canonical complex of a nonsingular plane cubic. Within a similar context in dimension 3, we exhibit in detail an interesting counterexample for a possible generalization of a theorem by Pan in which there exists a Sarkisov factorization obtained algorithmically that is not volume preserving.

papers.title: On the source algebra equivalence class of blocks with cyclic defect groups, II
papers.abstract:
This series of papers is a contribution to the program of classifying $p$-blocks of finite groups up to source algebra equivalence, starting with the case of cyclic blocks.
  To any $p$-block $\mathbf{B}$ of a finite group with cyclic defect group $D$, Linckelmann associated an invariant $W( \mathbf{B} )$, which is an indecomposable endo-permutation module over $D$, and which, together with the Brauer tree of $\mathbf{B}$, essentially determines its source algebra equivalence class. In Parts II-IV of our series of papers, we classify, for odd $p$, those endo-permutation modules of cyclic $p$-groups arising from $p$-blocks of quasisimple groups.
  In the present Part II, we reduce the desired classification for the quasisimple classical groups of Lie type $B$, $C$, and $D$ to the corresponding objective for the general linear and unitary groups; the classification is completed for the latter groups.

papers.title: On the Supersingular reduction of Cubic fourfolds with Complex Multiplication
papers.abstract: If $X$ is a K3 surface with complex multiplication by a CM field $E$, Kazuhiro Ito proved that the height of the reduction of $X$ in characteristic $p>0$, and its Artin invariant if it is supersingular, can be computed from the decomposition of $p$ in $E$. We present analogous results for cubic fourfolds by using the main theorem of complex multiplication for cubic fourfold, proved by Rikuto Ito.

papers.title: On the Witt liftability of quasi-F-split Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that a quasi-$F$-split strict Calabi--Yau variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of odd characteristic $p$ admits a smooth projective lifting over $W(k)$ if $p\geq d-1$, or if $p=d-2$ and $H^0(X,T_X)=0$. We also prove $W_3(k)$-liftability in odd characteristic.

papers.title: Parahoric Spherical Whittaker Functions
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_\mu$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor. Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation. We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$. In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.

papers.title: Partial Airy ideals and coloured blobbed topological recursion
papers.abstract: We define and study the notion of partial Airy ideals, which are certain linear systems of PDEs that may contain less equations than variables. We show that they admit a unique solution of exponential type (the partition function) modulo a choice of initial condition. We construct a large class of examples of partial Airy ideals attached to spectral curves using twisted free-field representations of $\mathcal{W}(\mathfrak{gl}_r)$-algebras at self-dual level. This generalizes the results of Bouchard- Borot-Chidambaram-Creutzig-Noshchenko by significantly enlarging the set of admissible spectral curves, provided they come with additional data that we call colour. We show that the differential constraints on the partition function are equivalent to a set of equations on the associated correlators, which we call coloured loop equations. We find a recursive residue formulation for the solutions of those equations, the coloured blobbed topological recursion}, which is a generalization of the currently known forms of topological recursion. It includes the blobbed topological recursion of Borot-Shadrin as a special case, giving it a natural interpretation within the formalism of partial Airy ideals.

papers.title: Partial Markov Categories
papers.abstract: We introduce partial Markov categories as a synthetic framework for synthetic probabilistic inference, blending the work of Cho and Jacobs, Fritz, and Golubtsov on Markov categories with the work of Cockett and Lack on cartesian restriction categories. We describe observations, Bayes' theorem, normalisation, and both Pearl's and Jeffrey's updates in purely categorical terms.

papers.title: PBW theorem for affine super Yangian
papers.abstract: We prove a Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the distinguished affine super Yangian $Y=Y_{1/2,1/2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n))$, where $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. With respect to the current filtration, there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{gr}_F Y\cong U\!\left(\operatorname{uce}\!\left( \mathfrak{sl}(m|n)\otimes\mathbb C[z^{\pm1},u] \right)\right), \] where $\operatorname{uce}$ denotes the universal central extension. For any totally ordered classical basis homogeneous in parity and current degree, ordered supermonomials in arbitrary fixed filtered lifts form a vector-space basis of $Y$, with odd exponents restricted to zero or one. The proof identifies the classical presentation through Steinberg Lie superalgebras and establishes injectivity using evaluation homomorphisms, iterated coproducts in degreewise completions, and coefficientwise tensor separation.

papers.title: Perverse filtration on the cohomology of affine Springer fibers
papers.abstract: We show that the top cohomology of any affine Springer fiber, as a Weyl group representation, contains a large part of the total cohomology of certain Springer fibers. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of a ``perverse filtration'' on the pure part of the cohomology of affine Springer fibers.

papers.title: Poincar\'e series of degree-two Chow varieties
papers.abstract: Let $C_{p, 2}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the Chow variety parametrizing effective algebraic $p$-cycles of degree two on $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. We show that its rational cohomology is pure Tate and concentrated in even degrees. An anti-invariant Chern class identity yields a presentation of the cohomology ring as a fiber product, which in turn determines the cohomology over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$. We identify the ordinary Poincar\'e polynomial with the known virtual formula, determine the optimal ranges over which the coefficients stabilize, and compute the nonrational Poincar\'e series of the stable space $D(2)$. For the Lawson--Michelsohn map $D(2)\longrightarrow D(\infty)$, the first nonzero rational homotopy kernel occurs in degree eight and is one-dimensional, while the integral kernel has rank one. Finally, we compute the relative homology of the pair $(D(2),BU)$ over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$ and show that additional cohomology generators and nonzero rational homotopy kernels arise in unbounded degrees.

papers.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
papers.abstract:
Let $X=V_5$ be the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Along the negative zero-tilt-slope paths for rational-curve ideal classes, degree five is the first degree admitting a positive point correction. We determine the resulting degree-five outer good moduli space: it is reduced with exactly two irreducible components, a normal ten-dimensional principal branch and a smooth corrected branch $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Their scheme-theoretic intersection is a normal determinantal ninefold. Along its singular locus, the principal branch has transverse rank-one $2\times 4$ determinantal singularities, while the intersection has the corresponding $2\times 3$ singularities.
  We construct an explicit small resolution of the principal branch as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petkovi\'c--Rota Kuznetsov-component sixfold along its point locus. Uniform wall exclusion and point-correction bounds for degrees two through five establish the first correction threshold; the corrected degree-five factors are precisely the ideals of elliptic linear sections parametrized by $\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$.

papers.title: Pointed Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of Hurwitz--Brill--Noether spaces with vanishing conditions at a totally ramified point. Degeneration to a curve with an elliptic tail simplifies the combinatorics of Larson, Larson--Larson--Vogt, and Aggarwal, giving inductive proofs of Aggarwal's results in the one-point setting, and yields an efficient recursion for the algebraic Euler characteristics. Finally, when the expected dimension is negative, we give a numerical criterion ensuring the universal Hurwitz--Brill--Noether locus admits a component of expected relative dimension, generically finite over its image in the Hurwitz space, analogous to the existing results of Pflueger and Teixidor i Bigas for classical Brill--Noether loci.

papers.title: Polynomial parametrization of quadratic Diophantine equations: decision and construction
papers.abstract: We give an algorithm that, for any polynomial with integer coefficients of degree at most two, decides whether its integer zero set is a finite union of polynomial families with integer coefficients and constructs such families whenever they exist. The main step is a constructive proof that, for every nondegenerate integral quadratic form \(Q\) isotropic over \(\mathbb{Q}\) and every integer \(m\), the integer solutions of \(Q(\mathbf{x})=m\) form a finite union of polynomial families. This proves the nondegenerate case of a result announced without proof by Vaserstein. For fixed \(Q\), the number of parameters in each family is bounded independently of \(m\). The new descent argument treats forms in at least five variables with rational Witt index one. We also settle the previously open cases \(zt-x^2-y^2=1\) and \(zt-x^2-y^2=-1\) by combining Larsen--Nguyen's group parametrization with a classical reduction of binary Hermitian forms, obtaining two and three polynomial families, respectively.

papers.title: Positive definite functions of noncommuting contractions, Hua-Bellman matrices, and a new distance metric
papers.abstract: We study positive definiteness of Hua-Bellman matrices (i.e., matrices of the form $[\det(I-A_i^*A_j)^{-α}]_{ij}$, where $A_i$ and $A_j$ are strict contractions and $α\in\mathbb{R}$). We start by revisiting a 1959 work of Bellman (Representation theorems and inequalities for Hermitian matrices; Duke Mathematical J., 26(3), 1959) that studies positive definiteness of Hua-Bellman matrices and claims a strengthening of Hua's representation-theoretic results (Inequalities involving determinants; Acta Mathematica Sinica, 5 (1955)). We uncover a critical error in Bellman's proof that has surprisingly escaped notice to date, and we show by an explicit example that his claim itself is false. We then provide conditions under which $\det(I-A^*B)^{-α}$ is a positive definite function. For complex contractions our condition is the known sharp one, with the integer exponents below Hua's range reached by an elementary argument. For real symmetric contractions we recover the part of Bellman's claims that survives. Building on our result, we introduce a new Poincaré-like distance metric on noncommuting strict contractions, and yet another `log-det' based distance in the appendix.

papers.title: Positivity of the Mirabolic Quantum Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct the canonical basis for the modified mirabolic quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. We then study the associated $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-module and $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-comodule structures and prove the positivity of this basis with respect to these two structures.

papers.title: Power-Kernel Fluctuations, the Lambert W Subpolynomial Source, and a Local CRT Conditional Law
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $n$ we define the power kernel $d_n = n/\operatorname{rad}(n)$ and the fluctuation $X_n = \log d_n$, where $\operatorname{rad}(n) = \prod_{p \mid n} p$. This paper develops three mutually supporting lines around this ``relative fluctuation''. First, the microscopic theory. From the kernel decomposition $n = v_d s$ ($s$ squarefree, $(s,d)=1$, $v_d = d \operatorname{rad}(d)$) we obtain the exact discrete law $\mathbb{P}(X_n = \log d) = \frac{6}{\pi^2} \frac{w(d)}{d \operatorname{rad}(d)}$, $w(d) := \prod_{p \mid d} \frac{p}{p+1}$, together with a three-branch parity-conditioned refinement. Parity is a first-order effect: the measured gap $\mathbb{E}[X_n \mid n \text{ even}] - \mathbb{E}[X_n \mid n \text{ odd}] = 0.69008$ matches $\log 2 = 0.69315$. Second, the conditional law. For fixed $c$, the distribution of $X_{c-a}$ is completely determined by $\mathrm{mask}(a)$ through a three-case local CRT convolution: the local contribution vanishes identically when $p \mid c$ or $p \mid a$, and otherwise follows a corrected law rather than the usual one, differing by a factor $\frac{p}{p-1}$ (a factor $2$ at $p=2$). The corrected law agrees with $220$ masks to $0.993$, while the usual law underestimates the tail by $47\%$--$78\%$. This replaces an earlier erroneous assertion of equidistribution. Third, the subpolynomial source. For radical-type Euler products $\prod_p \bigl(1 + \frac{\eta(p)}{p^\sigma - 1}\bigr)$ with $\eta(p) \to a$, one has as $\sigma \to 0^+$ the asymptotic $\Phi(\sigma) = \frac{a}{\sigma W(a/\sigma)}\bigl[1 + \frac{\kappa_1}{W} + \frac{\kappa_2}{W^2} + \cdots\bigr]$, where $W$ is the Lambert function. The main term comes not from small primes but from the prime range $[e^{v^*}, e^{1/\sigma}]$, which explains why no finite prime table can reproduce it. The coefficients satisfy $\kappa_n = (n-1)! + \sum_j c_{n,j} \zeta(2j)$, a sum over even zetas only, because the two-sided integral coefficients satisfy $\iota(r) = (-1)^{r+1} \rho(r)$, forcing odd-zeta terms to cancel exactly at every order. This unifies $T(x) = \sum_{n \le x} 1/\operatorname{rad}(n)$, $\Sigma(D)$ and $\Sigma_\perp(D;Q)$, and explains at one stroke why all previously fitted ``constants'' are transient. Applications include: a quantitative formula for Mazur parameters in the open range $1 < s < 2$ ($k_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1.91 \pm 0.17$, excluding $k=1,3$); the ceiling theorem $q \le \frac{\log c}{\log 2 + \log \operatorname{rad}(c)}$ (equality iff $\{a,b\} = \{1,2^k\}$); the rad--$P^+$ duality (principal versus negative Lambert branch); an exact $S$-unit reformulation of $\rho(c) = \min_a \operatorname{rad}(a)\operatorname{rad}(c-a)$; and a mechanistic decomposition of the exponent of $\mathcal{N}_0(N)$. We report honestly: the abc conjecture itself is not attackable within this framework. The three structural walls are: (i) the conditional law is provable for $D \le c^{1/2-\delta}$ while abc solutions live at $D \gtrsim c^{0.78}$; (ii) relaxing any one of the three radicals inflates the count by a factor $387$; (iii) the Fourier circle method is controllable iff $\alpha + \beta > 2$, while Mazur parameters always have $\alpha, \beta < 1$. Our weak abc bound is weaker than de Bruijn's 1962 trivial bound; this is recorded as well.

papers.title: Pre-modular fusion categories of global dimension $2p$
papers.abstract:
Let $p>5$ be a prime. In this paper, we show that a pre-modular fusion category of
  global dimension $2p$ is either pointed or tensor equivalent to $\text{Rep}(D_{2p})$.

papers.title: Prekosmic Grothendieck/Galois Categories
papers.abstract:
We establish a generalized version of the duality between groups and the categories of their representations on sets. Given an abstract symmetric monoidal category $K$ called Galois prekosmos, we define pre-Galois objects in $K$ and study the categories of their representations internal to $K$. The motivating example of $K$ is the cartesian monoidal category $\textit{Set}$ of sets, and pre-Galois objects in $\textit{Set}$ are groups. We present an axiomatic definition of pre-Galois $K$-categories, which is a complete abstract characterization of the categories of representations of pre-Galois objects in $K$. The category of covering spaces over a well-connected topological space is a prototype of a pre-Galois $\textit{Set}$-category. We establish a perfect correspondence between pre-Galois objects in $K$ and pre-Galois $K$-categories pointed with pre-fiber functors.
  We also establish a generalized version of the duality between flat affine group schemes and the categories of their linear representations. Given an abstract symmetric monoidal category $K$ called Grothendieck prekosmos, we define what are pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$ and study the categories of their representations internal to $K$. The motivating example of $K$ is the symmetric monoidal category $\textit{Vec}_k$ of vector spaces over a field $k$, and pre-Grothendieck objects in $\textit{Vec}_k$ are affine group $k$-schemes. We present an axiomatic definition of pre-Grothendieck $K$-categories, which is a complete abstract characterization of the categories of representations of pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$. The indization of a neutral Tannakian category over a field $k$ is a prototype of a pre-Grothendieck $\textit{Vec}_k$-category. We establish a perfect correspondence between pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$ and pre-Grothendieck $K$-categories pointed with pre-fiber functors.

papers.title: Process matrices on generalised theories
papers.abstract: We extend the process-matrix framework for defining indefinite causal orders to a broad class of generalised physical theories. We give a simple re-axiomatisation of spacetime contexts in terms of naturality over classical probes, which precisely captures non-contextual assignment together with compatibility with convexity and coarse-graining within local laboratories. Using this compositional perspective, we give a clean characterisation of theories in which abstract spacetime contexts admit a process-matrix representation, and we pin down the precise conditions (satisfied by classical theory, quantum theory, and a Boxworld-like theory) under which the supermap and process-matrix perspectives on higher-order processes coincide.

papers.title: Projected Brion's theorem
papers.abstract: We present an analogue of Brion's theorem for the projected integer-point transform. Brion's theorem writes the integer-point transform of a rational polyhedron $P$ as the sum of the rational functions associated to its vertex cones. The pushforward $\pi_*$ along a lattice projection $\pi$ turns the transform of $P$ into the generating function of the numbers of lattice points in the fibres of $\pi$. We group the vertices of $P$ into contracted classes, generated by the edges whose direction $\pi$ kills, and show that the sum of the rational functions associated to the vertex cones in a contracted class can be pushed forward along $\pi$, yielding a rational function decomposition of the projected integer-point transform. For a lattice polytope, the classes correspond to the connected components of the fixed locus of the associated toric variety under the action of a subtorus, and our formula resembles the localization formula for this subtorus. We use this decomposition to provide an explicit formula for the projected integer-point transform of a linear family of polytopes. We illustrate this result with families of Gelfand--Zetlin and string polytopes.

papers.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.

papers.title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
papers.abstract: We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.

papers.title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
papers.abstract: Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems. To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables. The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank. The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.

papers.title: Quivers with involutions and shifted twisted Yangians via Coulomb branches
papers.abstract: To a quiver with involution, we study the Coulomb branch of the 3d $\mathcal{N} = 4$ involution-fixed part of the quiver gauge theory. We show that there is an algebra homomorphism from the corresponding shifted twisted Yangian to the quantized Coulomb branch algebra. This gives a new instance of 3D mirror symmetries.

papers.title: Rank three representations of Painlev\'e systems: I. Wild character varieties
papers.abstract: We give explicit cubic equations for the wild character varieties corresponding to the rank 3 representations of Painlev\'e equations, and compare them to the ones of their classical rank 2 representations.

papers.title: Rank-Two Drinfeld Modules over Elliptic Coordinate Rings
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathbf A}$ be the affine coordinate ring of $E\setminus\{\infty\}$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $\infty$ is rational. We solve the rank-two case of the open problem of explicitly classifying sign-normalized Drinfeld ${\mathbf A}$-modules in generic characteristic with a fixed determinant motive; the classification for rank greater than two remains open. Outside an explicit exceptional locus, the rank-two Drinfeld modules are parametrized by the open modular curve $Y^{q+1}=\pi(X)$ with $Y\neq0$. The polynomial $\pi$ is squarefree, and the smooth projective completion of this curve has genus $q^2$. The roots of $\pi$ split into two types. Above roots of the first type, all coefficient functions extend regularly, and their extensions yield exactly the exceptional modules. Roots of the second type correspond to cusps of the modular curve; above these roots, the coefficient family has poles.

papers.title: Rational structures on quivers and a generalization of Gelfand's equivalence
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of rational structure on a quiver and associated representations to establish a coherent framework for studying quiver representations in separable field extensions. This notion is linked to a refinement of the notion of $K$-species, which we term \'etale $K$-species. We establish a categorical anti-equivalence between $K$-rational quivers and \'etale $K$-species, which extends to an equivalence of their respective representation categories. For $K$-rational quivers there is a canonical notion of base change, which suggests a corresponding notion of base change for (\'etale) $K$-species which we elaborate. As a primary application, we generalize Gelfand's celebrated equivalence between certain blocks of Harish-Chandra modules for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and representations of the Gelfand quiver to a rational setting. To this end, we define a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational structure on the Gelfand quiver and its representations. A key technical tool, which we call unipotent stabilization, is developed to construct the functor from rational Harish-Chandra modules to nilpotent rational quiver representations. We prove that this functor is an equivalence. A similar result is established for the cyclic quiver. Both results hold over every field $E$ of characteristic $0$, for suitable $E$-rational structures on the two quivers; for $E=\mathbb{C}$ they recover Gelfand's equivalence. In this rational framework the defining relation of the Gelfand quiver acquires a descent-theoretic meaning: its Galois orbit is stable, it descends to a single relation on the associated $\mathbb{Q}$-species, and a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational representation satisfies it if and only if the composite of the two arrows through the vertex $-$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational endomorphism of the space at the central vertex. This allows us to recast our results in the language of $\mathbb{Q}$-species.

papers.title: Relative $\mathbb{A}^1$-Contractibility of Koras-Russell Prototypes and Exotic Motivic Spheres
papers.abstract: The Koras-Russell threefolds are a certain family of smooth, affine contractible threefolds exhibiting "exotic" behavior in the algebro-geometric context. Our goal in this note is to extend its $\mathbb{A}^1$-contractibility from a field to a general base scheme. As a consequence, we also give a general strategy to extend the $\mathbb{A}^1$-contractibility of Koras-Russell prototypes in higher dimensions over a general base scheme. As a major consequence, we establish the existence of "exotic" motivic spheres in all dimensions at least 4 over infinite perfect fields.

papers.title: Riemannian three-manifolds as hypersurfaces of Euclidean four-space: the realizability operator, its symbol, and its linearisation at the round sphere
papers.abstract: For a Riemannian three-manifold $(\Sigma,g)$ with negative Einstein endomorphism $\mathbb{M}=-G$, the Gauss equation of a hypersurface of $\mathbb{R}^4$ reads $\mathbb{M}=\mathrm{adj}\,K$, and on $\{\det\mathbb{M}>0\}$ it is solved identically by $\tilde K=\sqrt{\det\mathbb{M}}\,\mathbb{M}^{-1}$. Realizability with nondegenerate second fundamental form is therefore the single equation $F(g)=\mathrm{Cod}(\tilde K(g))=0$. The reduction is classical (Beez, Killing, Thomas) and the zero set has been characterized intrinsically (Rivertz; Agaoka and Hashinaga); we study $F$ as a nonlinear operator on metrics. At every nondegenerate point its principal symbol has rank two, with kernel exactly the symbol of the linearised immersions, so $F$ is injective modulo immersions everywhere and nowhere elliptic modulo diffeomorphisms alone. The nine Codazzi components carry four identities, leaving five conditions at every nondegenerate point, and Cartan's test holds with equality, in exact arithmetic, off a proper real-algebraic set. On a closed manifold the zero set is nowhere dense in the nondegenerate domain. At the round $S^3$ the linearisation on transverse-traceless tensors is $\mathrm{Cod}\circ\frac{1}{2}(-\Delta+2)$, with singular values $n(n^2-1)/\sqrt{2}$ and $\|DF\,h\|^2\ge 288\|h\|^2$. For metrics foliated by round 2-spheres we solve the first-order problem in closed form and write down all hypersurfaces swept by round 2-spheres; the $\ell=1$ direction is realized exactly by tilting the spheres' 3-planes. We treat the degenerate locus by two polynomial forms, and give Gauss–Codazzi as the flatness of two $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ connections: on the nondegenerate domain, realizability is equivalent to a single parallel spinor. Every displayed result is checked by a deposited script.

papers.title: Safety of layered control systems via control barrier morphisms
papers.abstract: Layered control architectures provide a powerful paradigm for synthesizing controllers for complex systems. Yet, translating guarantees at each layer to system-level guarantees is challenging due to the interactions between layers. To address this problem, this paper presents a categorical perspective on layered control architectures. Individual systems are represented as control coalgebras, their interactions are specified as morphisms to mediators, and system-level behaviors are obtained via composition defined categorically as a pullback. To analyze the safety of these systems, we formulate control barrier morphisms (CBMs), the categorical generalization of control barrier functions. We prove that feedback controllers satisfying a CBM condition render the associated safe subobject forward invariant. It is through CBMs that we can establish the safety of layered systems: given a CBM at each layer subject to compatibility conditions, the universal property of the pullback implies the existence of a CBM for the composed system. Safety of a full-order model being safety filtered by a reduced-order model is recovered as a specialization of the categorical framework.

papers.title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla's special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of \cite[Remark 2.4]{BLMM17}, pointed out by Bruinier--Zuffetti \cite{BZ26}. Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily--Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work.

papers.title: Spectrahedral relaxations and tightenings of rigidly convex sets
