papers.abstract: We construct a natural spectrahedral relaxation of a rigidly convex set (rcs) that depends only on the cubic part and on the degree of the defining real zero polynomial. For quadratic polynomials, we prove exactness and for a product of linear polynomials, we show that a higher order version of our relaxation is exact. We also establish a way of tightening the relaxation by moving the origin inside the rcs, and that the rcs is recovered by sweeping the origin over its interior. To obtain all these results we use a linear form that is closely connected to the zeros of a given real zero polynomial. We also prove that any rcs can be written as an affine linear slice of the cone of non-negative polynomials. Using this, we can define a hierarchy of tightenings that are spectrahedral shadows. We can show that this tightening is exact if the given polynomial admits a determinantal representation. This tightening is similar to a tightening of a hyperbolicity cone due to Kummer, Plaumann, and Vinzant.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds of type K
papers.abstract: A Calabi-Yau threefold of type K is a free quotient $X=(S\times E)/G$ of the product of a K3 surface and an elliptic curve. We construct a family of geometric Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$ by using Liu's product construction on $S\times E$ and then inducing along the Galois covering. The family has dimension $2h^{1,1}(X)$, and is disjoint from the $\widetilde{\GL}_2^+(\R)$-orbit of Li's stability conditions. These threefolds carry a K3 fibration, and the pushforward of an object from a smooth K3 fiber is (semi)stable if and only if it is (semi)stable on the K3 surface.

papers.title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules
papers.abstract: Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules. In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules. In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schr\"oer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules. In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.

papers.title: Surfaces with canonical map of odd degree
papers.abstract:
Let $S$ be a smooth complex minimal surface of general type with $p_g:=h^0(K_S)\ge 4$ whose canonical map is generically finite of odd degree $d>1$ onto a surface $\Sigma$. We assume that the general canonical curve of $S$ is smooth and that $\Sigma$ is ruled by lines, and we prove:
  - $p_g\le d+2$
  - $\Sigma$ is a cone over the rational normal curve of degree $p_g-2$ in ${\mathbb P}^{p_g-1}$
  - $p_g=d+2$ can occur only for $d=3,9,11$.
  As a byproduct, we refine previous results by Beauville and Xiao by proving that if one drops the assumption that $\Sigma$ is ruled by lines then $d\le 5$ if $p_g\ge 112$.
  The case $d=3$ being completely classified by the first two named authors, we focus on $d=5$, showing that $p_g\le 5$ and that for $p_g=5$ the surface $S$ has a pencil $|C|$ with $C^2=1$ and $K_SC=5$.
  These results suggest that the answer to the question whether the surfaces with canonical map of odd degree $d>1$ have bounded invariants could be positive, in sharp contrast with the case of even degree.

papers.title: Symmetric List Objects
papers.abstract: Cons-lists are fundamental to functional programming, and are well-understood as initial algebras, and as a concrete construction of free monoids. In category theory, such list objects can be axiomatised internal to any monoidal category, with nil and cons maps, and a recursion mechanism. When strengthened to support parametrised recursion, they can be shown to give the free monoid construction. We study a small variant on parametrised list objects called parametrised symmetric list objects, in a symmetric monoidal category, where the two frontmost elements are allowed to be permuted. We show that this gives a construction of free commutative monoids, and develop some related theory.

papers.title: Symmetric Volume Descent from U4 and a Four-Dimensional Lower Bound
papers.abstract: We explain a symmetric deformation that decreases the volume of the four-dimensional constant-width body $U_4$. The emphasis is on why the deformation works, rather than the size of the decrease. Oddness preserves width; convexity requires control of the curvature radii. A positive cap on one support branch is coupled to a negative correction on the adjacent branch. Their first-order volume contributions have different orders in the localization parameter, so the favorable contribution dominates. A small motion towards the ball makes the direction feasible for positive time. In a separate part we give a spectral lower bound for all four-dimensional bodies of constant width one, including an explicit positive refinement. A short projection argument using a three-dimensional theorem of Jiang gives the stronger lower bound $0.17872203$. A substantial gap between the lower and upper bounds remains.

papers.title: Syzygy-Quiver Formulas and Finitistic Dimensions of Special Biserial Algebras
papers.abstract:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite dimensional algebra over a field $\mathbf{k}$. We introduce the reachable syzygy quiver of $\Lambda$, a directed multigraph whose vertices are the isomorphism classes of indecomposable nonprojective direct summands of iterated syzygies of simple modules, and whose arrows record nonprojective summands of first syzygies. The projective dimension of a vertex is one plus its directed path height, allowing the global and finitistic dimensions of $\Lambda$ to be read off from this height function. This formula holds for every finite dimensional algebra, but its states are arbitrary modules.
  We show that when the first syzygy of an indecomposable module admits a closed combinatorial description from the bound quiver, this state space reduces to a smaller combinatorial quiver, making the global and finitistic dimensions exact computable invariants. We carry this out in three stages. Over a special biserial algebra, the Liu--Morin closure theorem identifies the reachable syzygy quiver with a string-syzygy quiver whose vertices are string modules. Over a string algebra, this compresses to the relation-chain quiver of Xin and Zhang, recovering their global dimension formula along with a parallel formula for the finitistic dimension. Over an arbitrary biserial algebra, the universal formula holds, but uniform compression to paths or strings is impossible, with the Skowro\'nski--Waschb\"usch algebra providing a witness. Finally, we show two string algebras may share the same Gabriel quiver but have distinct global dimensions, proving the ideal of relations is indispensable for these invariants, and we prove that a pointwise homological reduction to a string algebra on the same quiver preserving the monomials of the relations is impossible.

papers.title: Tensor products of 2-representations
papers.abstract: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.

papers.title: Test ideals can be computed by boundaries
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a normal $F$-finite ring of characteristic $p>0$. We show that one effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $\Delta$, with $K_R+\Delta$ $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$, computes the big test ideal. This answers a question of Schwede and Smith. More generally, we prove their conjecture that test module of a Cartier algebra acting on an ideal is the test module of a single map $\psi$ in the algebra and even the image of $\psi$. We prove a global version for schemes quasi-projective over an $F$-finite local ring as well. In particular, every such normal, locally strongly $F$-regular scheme admits an effective boundary $\Delta$ for which $(X,\Delta)$ is locally strongly $F$-regular and $K_X+\Delta$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$.
authors: with Appendix joint with Daniel Apsley

papers.title: The $\mathbf{P}^1$-motivic Gysin map
papers.abstract: We develop a $\mathbf{P}^1$-unstable non-$\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant theory of motivic spaces and spectra, and construct the Gysin map therein for regular immersions. This in particular gives the Gysin map in the Annala--Hoyois--Iwasa $\mathbf{P}^1$-motivic spectra, and thus gives a uniform construction for the Gysin maps of various cohomology theories.

papers.title: The $q$-deformed random-to-random family in the Hecke algebra
papers.abstract:
We generalize Reiner--Saliola--Welker's well-known but mysterious family of *$k$-random-to-random shuffles* from Markov chains on symmetric groups to Markov chains on Type-$A$ Iwahori--Hecke algebras. We prove that these operators pairwise commute, and that their eigenvalues are polynomials in $q$ with non-negative integer coefficients; we express these eigenvalues in a closed form as certain symmetric function evaluations (which is new even for $q=1$). We show that these operators are simultaneously diagonalizable for almost all $q$, and combinatorially express the dimension of the subalgebra they generate.
  Our work generalizes and extends work of Reiner--Saliola--Welker and Lafreni\`ere for the symmetric group, and simplifies all known proofs in this case.

papers.title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
papers.abstract:
We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$.
  We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.

papers.title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity. The main analytic difficulty is to obtain estimates uniform over lattices of unbounded determinant. We address this by combining a reduction based on primitive sublattices of codimension one and least determinant with explicit bounds for theta norms and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.

papers.title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $\phi$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $\rho$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_\rho$, $\overline{\Delta}_\rho$, $IC_\rho$, and $\delta_\rho$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp!}\pi$, and $i_{b!*}\pi$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $\pi$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $\phi$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.

papers.title: The classification of quasi-elliptic fibrations and unexpected plane cubics in characteristics 2 and 3
papers.abstract: In this paper, we categorize all isomorphism classes of quasi-elliptic surfaces over a field $k$ of characteristic 2 or 3. For every quasi-elliptic surface $X$, we classify all possible sequences of blow-downs from $X$ to the projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2_k$. We then use these categorizations to identify all unexpected plane cubic curves in characteristic 2 and present a proof of the lack of unexpected cubics in characteristic 3. Before the work in this paper -- based partly on the author's thesis -- the complete classification of unexpected plane cubic curves in characteristic 2 was unknown, as well as the question of the existence of unexpected plane cubic curves in characteristic 3.

papers.title: The Cone Conjecture for Enriques Surfaces in any Characteristic
papers.abstract: We give a proof of the Morrison-Kawamata cone conjecture for Enriques surfaces independent of their characteristic. It is based on the analysis of certain generically finite morphisms of degree two.

papers.title: The derived length of subgroups of the Cremona group
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal derived length of a solvable subgroup of the plane Cremona group over $\mathbb C$ is equal to $5$. The main difficulty is the case of subgroups containing loxodromic elements. To treat this case, we prove that the maximal derived length of a finite solvable subgroup is $4$ and establish a centraliser theorem: the centraliser of a finite solvable subgroup of derived length $4$ contains no loxodromic element. The proof of the centraliser theorem relies on Blanc's classification of maximal algebraic subgroups and then uses equivariant Sarkisov theory, orbit estimates, superrigidity, and fixed curves of genus at least two.

papers.title: The Einstein-Hilbert functional and the Donaldson-Futaki invariant
papers.abstract: Given a Kaehler manifold polarised by a holomorphic ample line bundle, we consider the circle bundle associated to the polarisation with the induced transversal holomorphic structure. The space of contact structures compatible with this transversal structure is naturally identified with a bundle, of infinite rank, over the space of Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein-Hilbert functional of the associated Tanaka-Webster connections is a functional on this bundle, whose critical points are constant scalar curvature Sasaki structures. In particular, when the group of automorphisms is discrete, these critical points correspond to constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein--Hilbert functional satisfies some monotonicity properties along some one-parameter families of CR-contact structures that are naturally associated to test configurations, and that its limit on the central fibre of a test configuration is related to the Donaldson-Futaki invariant through an expansion in terms of an extra real parameter. As a by-product, we obtain an original proof that the existence of constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics on a polarized manifold implies K-semistability. We also show that the limit of the Einstein-Hilbert functional on the central fibre coincides with the ratio of the equivariant index characters pole coefficients of the central fibre.

papers.title: The geometry of solutions to the general sextic
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of the three simplest known formulas for roots of a general sextic polynomial. In contrast with work of Green on the quintic, we show that no "simultaneous uniformization" of the normal forms associated to the solutions exists. This demonstrates an intrinsic qualitative complexity of sextic equations that is not present in quintic equations. Additionally, we give a formula for the roots of a general sextic in terms of Hilbert modular cusp forms and the uniformizing differential equation of the associated Hilbert modular surface.

papers.title: The inverse local-relative correspondence and the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation
papers.abstract: We prove the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation for the local Gromov--Witten theory of smooth weak del Pezzo surfaces, by identifying its unique formal solution with the inverse of the local-relative correspondence. We construct this inverse through an associative set-partition convolution and establish the identification using Zagier's recursion for the Bloch--Okounkov $n$-point function. The proof applies in all genera and includes non-toric surfaces.

papers.title: The Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in dimensions three and four
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, confirming the Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.

papers.title: The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$
papers.abstract: We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two. We also prove numerical dimension zero and construct the unique projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal minimal model. Its Picard number is one and its canonical divisor has order two. The perfect cone compactification is a Mori dream space, and the birational automorphism group of $\mathcal{A}_6$ is trivial. The proof combines normal vanishing on the Prym locus, polar intersections on abelian boundary fibers, and an exact theta calculation. A discrepancy estimate recovers the modular open subset from the minimal model.

papers.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
papers.abstract: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting K\"ahler-Ricci solitons. It recovers the usual Miyaoka-Yau inequality in the K\"ahler-Einstein case. Our proof uses weighted equivariant Bogomolov-Gieseker and Langer inequalities for torsion-free sheaves, together with a weighted slope estimate for the canonical extension sheaf. We also construct toric examples showing that the existence of a soliton implies neither weighted semistability of the canonical extension sheaf nor nonnegativity of the equivariant Miyaoka-Yau number.

papers.title: The Multivariable Strong Monodromy Conjecture for Plane Curves
papers.abstract: We prove the multivariable Strong Monodromy Conjecture for the local topological zeta function of arbitrary tuples of nonzero nonunit plane curve germs. The entries may be nonreduced and may have common irreducible factors. We also prove that the non-equivariant local motivic and topological zeta functions have the same polar locus and generic pole orders, using a multivariable extension of the Nicaise--Xu definition of motivic pole order. Our arguments combine twisted Poincar\'e residues with resolution formulas and specialization to one variable. In arbitrary dimension, we prove that a nonzero iterated residue class on a stratum of a log resolution implies the vanishing of the Bernstein--Sato ideal at the corresponding parameter. In particular, every topological polar hyperplane whose order equals the ambient dimension is contained in this zero locus. For algebraic germs, the topological pole order is at most the motivic pole order, and the two attain maximal order simultaneously.

papers.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
papers.abstract:
We investigate counting problems for discrete (geometric) structures in tropical settings, motivated by the comparison of the expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games.
  First, we give an upper bound on the number of coherent matching fields of type $(n,r)$ and a lower bound on the number of combinatorial types of $n$-hyperplane sequences in the max-plus tropical space of dimension $r-1$. These structures are closely related, and our bounds establish that as $n \to \infty$, for every fixed $r$ their number equals $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$. This in turn implies that the number of regular triangulations of the products of simplices $\Delta^{n-1}\times\Delta^{r-1}$ is also $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$, thereby answering a question of Santos.
  Second, we obtain that the number of labeled order types over the reals and over the signed tropical numbers coincide at first order, establishing a comparison of the expressivity of mean-payoff games and linear programs as measured by labeled order types.
  Last, the subclass of mean-payoff games known as parity games arise from linear programs by a ``double tropicalization.'' We show that the number of labeled order types obtained after this double tropicalization collapses.

papers.title: The Poincar\'e polynomial of the type B analogue of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n+1}$
papers.abstract: We establish formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomial of the type B analogue of the Deligne--Knudsen--Mumford moduli space of rational curves with n marked points, providing type B counterparts to results by Keel, Manin, Getzler, and Yuzvinsky. We establish functional and differential equations satisfied by the bivariate exponential generating function of these polynomials. We show how this generating function relates to the classical one in type A. We deduce the gamma-positivity of these polynomials via a quadratic recursion and discuss a type B analogue of a formula found by Aluffi, Marcolli and Nascimento in type A.

papers.title: The random graph ideal and fractional coloring
papers.abstract: The random graph ideal is pathological, answering a question of López-Abad et al. We prove this by constructing a positive hereditarily pathological restriction using Kneser graphs. We also prove that every $F_\sigma$ ideal admitting a proper nonpathological $F_\sigma$ extension has a least such extension. Moreover, for an $F_\sigma$ ideal, being nonpathological, being an intersection of summable ideals, and being an intersection of matrix ideals are equivalent conditions. This answers both converses asked by Filipów and Tryba. The least nonpathological $F_\sigma$ extension of the random graph ideal is proper and is described by the fractional cochromatic numbers of its finite induced subgraphs.

papers.title: Three cubic trinomial series for $1/\pi$
papers.abstract: We prove the three identities in Sun's Conjecture VI, involving cubes of generalized central trinomial coefficients. A common double integral represents their generating functions. On two rational curves, this period reduces to quadratic expressions in Gauss hypergeometric functions associated with elliptic integrals. A first-order identity recovers the derivative transverse to each curve and supplies the linear weights in the three series. The constants are determined by an endpoint calculation and Bauer's identity. Classical modular equations of degrees three, five, and seven then complete the evaluations. We give explicit rational differential certificates for the period reductions and the transverse derivative identities.

papers.title: Topology of irregular isomonodromy times on a fixed pointed curve
papers.abstract: We will define and study (moduli) spaces of deformations of irregular classes on Riemann surfaces, which provide an intrinsic viewpoint on the `times' of irregular isomonodromy systems in general. Our aim is to study the deeper generalisation of the G-braid groups that occur as fundamental groups of such deformation spaces, with particular focus on the generalisation of the full G-braid groups.

papers.title: Torsion Theories in a non-pointed Context II: iterated torsion theories
papers.abstract: Generalizing a known result in the context of homological categories, we show that, in a regular protomodular category $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a posetal, monocoreflective subcategory whose coreflector inverts monomorphisms, every torsion theory, in a non-pointed sense, satisfying suitable properties gives rise to a torsion theory in the category $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ of arrows in $\mathcal{C}$. Moreover, we show that the induced torsion theory in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ satisfies the same good properties of the original one in $\mathcal{C}$, allowing to iterate the process. Examples of this situation can be found in protomodular varieties of universal algebras with more than one constant or in duals of elementary toposes.

papers.title: Total positivity in coordinate algebras
papers.abstract: We define the totally positive part of the coordinate algebra associated to a Cartan datum of simply laced type. We show its relation to the canonical basis of the corresponding plus part of the enveloping algebra.

papers.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang's descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, K\"ahler--Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture.

papers.title: Universal Support Theorems for Resilient Coverage
papers.abstract: We prove that one finite set of points decides whether sensors cover a polygonal target under every failure rule in which an extra working sensor never hurts. The set is the same for every such rule, and on a face of dimension f the weakest point is fixed by f+1 sensors. The theorem holds in any dimension for functions that share a convex part and differ by affine terms. For sensing disks it gives the exact radius and power that keep the target covered under each rule, as rational numbers, the full trade-off between radius and budget, the smallest list of sensor groups whose loss breaks coverage, exact tests under independent placement errors, and protection plans proved optimal by a matching dual certificate.

papers.title: Unsupervised Topological Characterization of Slug, Churn and Annular Flow in Small-Diameter Vertical Pipes Using Euler Characteristic Surfaces
papers.abstract: Regime transitions in vertical gas-liquid flow are read from mechanistic models or assigned by eye, and for churn flow neither route has produced a settled criterion. We ask how much an unsupervised topological description of flow video can establish about them. The description is the Euler characteristic surface, a count of the connected gas and liquid regions in each frame across morphological scales. Kernels derived from it are combined by unsupervised multiple kernel learning, and the trials are divided into contiguous groups along gas velocity. For 37 air-water trials in 2-in. tubing at one liquid rate, with three viewing stations averaged, four groups are separated at 4.33, 7.51 and 11.70 m/s. Each division falls at or within one trial of a change in the visual evaluation of the same videos; cuts placed at random would match as closely in 12% of cases. The divisions move between viewing stations and under resampling, a kernel built on gas velocity divides any sampled range into roughly equal parts and cannot locate a transition, and the data do not support a revised transition criterion. On independent images from an annulus, churn shows about three times the across-scale variance of slug. Within the band the published criteria assign to churn, the two upper cuts fall at graded changes in the rankings, consistent with a progression within churn; if confirmed by further data, they would subdivide the churn region.

papers.title: Volumes of moduli spaces of flat surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the moduli spaces of flat surfaces with prescribed conical singularities. Veech showed that these spaces are diffeomorphic to the moduli spaces of marked Riemann surfaces, and endowed with a natural volume form depending on the orders of the singularities. We show that the volumes of these spaces are finite. Moreover we show that they are explicitely computable by induction on the Euler characteristics of the punctured surface for almost all orders of the singularities.

papers.title: Wall divisors on irreducible symplectic orbifolds of Nikulin-type
papers.abstract: We determine the wall divisors on irreducible symplectic orbifolds which are deformation equivalent to a special type of examples, called Nikulin orbifolds. The Nikulin orbifolds are obtained as partial resolutions in codimension 2 of a quotient by a symplectic involution of a Hilbert scheme of 2 points on a K3 surface. This builds on the previous article arXiv:2009.04873 in which the theory of wall divisors was generalized to orbifold singularities.

papers.title: Webs and finite dimensional representation theory for quantum symmetric pairs
papers.abstract: We develop a highest weight framework and construct explicit finite dimensional irreducible modules for the type AIII (quasi split) quantum symmetric pair subalgebras $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$. In Part 1, we provide a uniform construction of Cartan subalgebras and Verma modules for both subfamilies. Our construction recovers Letzter's Cartan subalgebra in one subfamily and gives a new Cartan subalgebra in the other. We construct a weak triangular decomposition of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$ via the Letzter map. Then we define Verma modules as induced modules and prove that finite dimensional simple $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$-modules are quotients of our Verma modules. In Part 2, we define a diagrammatic category $Web^B$ that controls polynomial representations of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$. We prove a multiplicity-free decomposition of the quantum exterior powers $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$ as a $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$-module, using a explicit eigenspace decomposition of certain dot morphisms in $Web^B$. As applications, we deduce the multiplicity-freeness of the involved anti-spherical Hecke module. For $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$, we explicitly determine the highest weight vectors and their weights, thereby determining the isomorphism classes of their irreducible summands. Finally, we determine the kernel of the $Web^B$-action on certain finite dimensional representation category of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$.
